column3: Mother's brother, your maternal uncle. The family words keep the two sides of the family apart: 叔叔 and 伯伯 are on the father's side, and 舅舅 is the mother's. 舅 has 男 "man" for the meaning and 臼 for the sound (jiù, the same). The second syllable is neutral.
column7: My uncle on my mother's side lives in Taichung.

column3: Wife of the mother's brother, your maternal uncle's wife, in speech. Written 舅媽 in Taiwan, and the second part is read mā here, as in 媽媽 "mother", with the woman 女 on its left. The uncle is 舅舅.
column6: Jiùmā jīntiān zuò le hěn duō cài.
column7: My aunt cooked a lot of dishes today.

column3: Paternal grandfather, the formal word, for writing and for introductions: 我的祖父. In speech you say 爺爺. 祖 is "ancestor" and 父 "father". 祖 has 礻 "altar, spirit" on the left, and 且, which began as a picture of an altar and is where the character comes from.
column7: My grandfather is eighty this year.

column3: Paternal grandmother, the formal word: 我的祖母. At home you say 奶奶. 祖 "ancestor" + 母 "mother". It is for the father's mother only; the mother's mother is 外祖母 or 外婆.
column7: Grandmother likes to grow flowers.

column3: Maternal grandfather, the formal word. 外 "outside" marks the mother's side, so it is 外 + 祖父. In speech, 外公 is used. You see it in writing and on forms, and when an elder is introduced formally.
column7: My maternal grandfather was a teacher.

column3: Maternal grandmother, the formal word for your mother's mother, built from 外 "outside" + 祖母. In speech people say 外婆, and in writing 外祖母. Pair it with 外祖父.
column7: My maternal grandmother is seventy this year.

column3: Ancestors, the people of past generations in a family or a people: 拜祖先 "pay respects to the ancestors", a Taiwan custom at New Year and at the Qingming festival. 祖 "ancestor" + 先 "earlier". In biology it can mean the ancestral species.
column4: 过年的时候我们要拜祖先。
column5: 過年的時候我們要拜祖先。
column6: Guònián de shíhou wǒmen yào bài zǔxiān.
column7: At New Year we pay respects to our ancestors.

column3: Sisters, both older and younger: 姊 "older sister" + 妹 "younger sister". 我有兩個姊妹. Family: 兄弟姊妹 "brothers and sisters". It is also used for linked things, such as 姊妹市 "sister city" and 姊妹校. Taiwan writes 姊 where the mainland has 姐.
column7: I have three sisters.

column3: Baby, small child and "doll". As a doll it is 洋娃娃 "foreign doll". Used also for a baby-faced look: 娃娃臉. It is a doubled word with a neutral second syllable. 娃 has 女 for the meaning and 圭 for the sound.
column4: 她给女儿买了一个娃娃。
column5: 她給女兒買了一個娃娃。
column6: Tā gěi nǚ'ér mǎi le yī ge wáwa.
column7: She bought her daughter a doll.

column3: In school it means "a new student, a freshman": 大學新生, 新生訓練 "orientation". 新生 also means "newborn" (新生兒, 新生命) and "new, emerging" in writing. 新 "new" + 生 "born, student".
column7: The school welcomes the new students.

column3: Lover, sweetheart: 情 "feeling" + 人 "person". It points to a romantic partner and has a poetic flavor; 男朋友 and 女朋友 are the everyday words. 情人節 is Valentine's Day.
column7: They are a pair of lovers.

column3: To be heartbroken, to break up, from 失 "lose" + 戀 "love". The speaker says 我失戀了. It is used for the person who was left or whose love ended; it needs no object. 戀 has 心 "heart" under it, as 愛 does. 戀愛 is "romantic love".
column6: Tā shīliàn le, xīnqíng bù hǎo.
column7: He has broken up with someone and is in a bad mood.

column3: Single, unmarried or without a partner: 我還是單身. 單 "single" + 身 "body". Used with 還 or 仍 in 仍然單身. You can ask 你單身嗎？ This is a normal, polite question in Taiwan.
column7: I am still single.

column3: Marriage as a state or institution: 婚姻幸福 "a happy marriage", 婚姻狀況 "marital status" on forms. The verb "to marry" is 結婚, not this word. Both characters have 女 "woman" at the left.
column7: Their marriage is very happy.

column3: Fickle in love, unfaithful: 他很花心 "he plays around". It describes someone, usually a man, with many relationships, and it is a criticism. Literally "flower heart"; the same two characters can mean the center of a flower.
column7: I heard he is unfaithful.

column3: To cherish, to treasure, to use with care, for things you do not want to waste: 愛惜時間 "make good use of time", 愛惜東西 "take care of things", 愛惜身體. It does not mean love for a person. 惜 has the heart mark 忄 and 昔 as the sound (xī).
column7: You should make good use of your time.

column3: To make friends: 交 "mix, make" + 友 "friend". It is written style: 交友網站 "friend-making sites", and on dating apps 交友軟體. In speech people say 交朋友. 交友要小心 is a warning.
column7: Be careful when making friends online.

column3: Feeling, emotion, and "situation". It occurs in compounds: 感情 "feelings, relationship", 愛情 "romantic love", 友情 "friendship", 心情 "mood", 事情 "matter". In 事情 the 情 is neutral. 忄 "heart" is the meaning part.
column7: They get along very well.

column3: Congratulations: 恭喜你！ or 恭喜恭喜！ Used for a wedding, a new baby, a promotion or a new year. For New Year 恭喜發財 is said. 恭 means "respectful" and 喜 "joy".
column7: Congratulations on getting into university!

column3: To get rich, a verb with its object: 發了財. It is heard at New Year in the greeting 恭喜發財 "may you get rich". 發財 can also describe a business booming. 發 "send out" + 財 "wealth", where 貝 "shell" stands for money.
column7: Happy New Year, may you prosper!

column3: As one wishes, satisfactory: 萬事如意 "may everything go as you wish", a standard New Year wish. 如 "like, as" + 意 "intention". Also a 如意 is a ceremonial scepter that is a symbol of good luck.
column7: I wish you all the best.

column3: Firecrackers: 放鞭炮 "set off firecrackers". Taiwan has them at New Year, at temple festivals and at weddings, to scare away bad luck. 鞭 "whip" + 炮 "cannon, cracker". 炮 has 火 "fire" and 包 for the sound.
column4: 过年的时候大家放鞭炮。
column5: 過年的時候大家放鞭炮。
column6: Guònián de shíhou dàjiā fàng biānpào.
column7: At New Year everybody sets off firecrackers.

column3: In Taiwan, "fireworks": 放煙火 "set off fireworks", 看煙火, and the New Year's Eve show at Taipei 101 is 跨年煙火. The mainland says 烟花. The older meaning is "smoke and fire" or "cooked food", as in 人間煙火. 煙 "smoke" has 火 on its left.
column4: 跨年的时候可以看烟火。
column5: 跨年的時候可以看煙火。
column6: Kuànián de shíhou kěyǐ kàn yānhuǒ.
column7: On New Year's Eve you can watch fireworks.

column3: To reunite, of a family: 一家團圓. At the New Year's Eve dinner, the 團圓飯, the whole family comes together. 團 and 圓 both mean "round", with an enclosure 囗 around them, which suits a family circle. 圓 has 員 as the sound (yuán).
column4: 过年时，全家人都回来团圆。
column5: 過年時，全家人都回來團圓。
column6: Guònián shí, quánjiārén dōu huílái tuányuán.
column7: At New Year the whole family comes home for a reunion.

column3: To entertain, host, treat: 招待客人 "look after guests", and as a noun "hospitality", as in 謝謝你的招待. Used when the host pays or serves: 今天我招待你 "it's my treat". 招 means "beckon, invite" and has 扌 "hand".
column7: Thank you for your hospitality.

column3: Rose. 玫瑰花 is the flower, counted with 朵 (a single flower) or 束 (a bunch). Given on Valentine's Day. Both characters have 玉 "jade" on the left, since they were first words for a kind of gem; 瑰 has 鬼 as the sound (guǐ and guī).
column6: Tā sòng le tā yī duǒ méiguī.
column7: He gave her a rose.

column3: Eat, drink and be merry, a four-character idiom about a life of pleasure. It is often negative: 他只知道吃喝玩樂 "all he cares about is having fun". The 樂 here is read lè "happy", not yuè "music".
column4: 他每天只知道吃喝玩乐。
column5: 他每天只知道吃喝玩樂。
column7: All he does every day is eat, drink and have fun.

column3: An interjection of surprise, dissatisfaction or calling attention: 哎，你的鑰匙掉了！ 哎呀 is a stronger form. Unlike 唉, which is a sigh, 哎 is a sudden reaction or a call. The 口 "mouth" tells you it is a sound.
column6: Āi, nǐ de yàoshi diào le!
column7: Hey, you dropped your key!

column3: A sigh of disappointment or sadness: 唉，今天又下雨了. It can also be a short "yes" to a call: 小明！唉！ It sounds like 哎 and both have 口, but 唉 is for feeling low and 哎 for a surprise or a call.
column7: Sigh, it's raining again today.

column3: Hi, a casual greeting borrowed from English, between friends and young people: 嗨，你好！ It is lighter than 你好 and not for formal meetings. The characters only give the sound: 口 "mouth" and 海 "sea". In some uses it also means "high", as in happy or excited.
column7: Hi, how are you?

column3: Two uses in Taiwan. As an interjection: "oh, I see", when you understand something: 喔，我知道了. And at the end of a sentence it softens the tone, as a gentle reminder: 小心喔 "be careful, okay", 好喔 "okay". The second use is very typical of Taiwan speech. 哦 is a similar interjection with another tone.
column7: Oh, I see.

column3: An interjection of doubt or surprise, with a rising tone: 哦？真的嗎？ It can also show that you have just understood something, with a falling tone, and Taiwan often writes that as 喔. Unlike 喔 it is not placed at the end of a sentence to soften it. 口 "mouth" and 我 for the sound.
column7: Oh, so it's you!

column3: A particle at the end of a sentence which says "this is obvious" or "of course", sometimes with a little impatience, or a wish to be persuaded: 這是你自己說的嘛 "you said it yourself", 好嘛 "come on, okay". It also marks a pause after a topic: 你嘛，就別去了. 口 "mouth" and 麻 for the sound.
column6: Zhè shì nǐ zìjǐ shuō de ma.
column7: But you said it yourself.

column3: A hum which shows that you are listening or that you agree, like "mm-hm" or "yes": 嗯，我同意. With a rising tone it asks "huh?", and with a falling tone it can show doubt or a quiet yes. The tone changes with the meaning, which is why the dictionary gives it a neutral tone.
column7: Mm, I agree.

column3: Two uses. "That's right!", as an answer: 對了！就是這樣. And "oh, by the way", to bring up something you just remembered: 對了，你明天有空嗎？ Context tells them apart: at the start of a sentence, followed by a new topic, it is the second.
column6: Duìle, nǐ míngtiān yǒu kòng ma?
column7: Oh, by the way, are you free tomorrow?

column3: Forget it, never mind, let it go: 算了，不要吵了. You say it to drop a subject, to give up on something, or to tell someone not to worry about it. 算 "count" and 了 "finished", so the matter is counted as closed. It can sound resigned or a little annoyed.
column7: Forget it, we'll go next time.

column3: No wonder: 難怪你這麼累 "no wonder you are so tired". It comes after you learn a reason, and says that now the result is no surprise. It is followed by the result, often with a particle or 這麼. 難 "hard" + 怪 "blame, strange".
column7: No wonder you are so tired.

column3: Needless to say: 不用說，他一定會來 "needless to say, he will come". It marks something that is obvious. 不用說 can also mean "no need to speak", as in 你不用說了. 不用 means "need not" and 說 "say".
column7: Needless to say, he will come.

column3: Rice vermicelli, thin noodles of rice flour. In Taiwan, 炒米粉 "fried rice noodles" and 米粉湯 "rice noodle soup" are everyday dishes, and 新竹米粉 from Hsinchu is well known. It can also mean rice flour. 米 is a picture of grains of rice, and 粉 "powder" has 米 as its meaning part.
column7: I'd like to eat fried rice noodles.

column3: Noodles, wheat noodles of any kind, as opposed to 米粉. Taiwan writes it 麵條, with the noodle character 麵, so that it is not confused with 面 "face". 一碗麵 "a bowl of noodles", 牛肉麵 "beef noodles", 吃麵 "eat noodles". 條 is a measure word for long thin things, and fits noodles.
column7: I'd like to eat noodles for lunch.

column3: Boiled dumplings. In Taiwan 水餃 are boiled and 鍋貼 are pan-fried, and the two are sold in the same shops. Counted by number: 十個水餃, and you can make them with 包水餃 "wrap dumplings". 餃 has 食 "food" on the left and 交 for the sound.
column7: Let's make dumplings.

column3: Vinegar, used for dipping dumplings and in many sauces: 沾醋 "dip in vinegar". 吃醋 "eat vinegar" means "to be jealous", especially in love. 酉 on the left is a wine jar, since vinegar is sour wine; 昔 is the sound part.
column7: Dumplings are eaten dipped in vinegar.

column3: Soy sauce: 醬 "sauce" + 油 "oil". The word for table use. Dark soy sauce, 醬油, is the usual kind in Taiwanese cooking; 醬油膏 is a thicker, sweeter kind used for dipping. 醬 has 酉 "wine jar" below it, as fermented foods do.
column7: Please give me a little soy sauce.

column3: Taste, preference in flavor: 口味重 "likes strong flavors", 口味清淡 "likes light food", 合我的口味 "suits my taste". Also the "flavor" of a product, as on drinks and chips: 什麼口味？ 口 "mouth" + 味 "taste".
column6: Zhè dào cài hěn hé wǒ de kǒuwèi.
column7: This dish suits my taste.

column3: To cook, boil, usually by heating in water: 煮飯 "cook rice", 煮麵 "cook noodles", 煮水 "boil water", 煮咖啡. 炒 stir-fries and 烤 bakes, and 煮 is the general word. 灬 "fire" is at the bottom and 者 on top.
column6: Wǒ lái zhǔ fàn, nǐ qù mǎi cài.
column7: I'll cook, you go and buy groceries.

column3: Cook, chef: 廚 "kitchen" + 師 "master". 師 ends the name of many skilled professions: 老師, 醫師, 律師. 廚師 is a professional cook in a restaurant or hotel, and a home cook is described differently, as with 做飯 "cook".
column4: 这家餐厅的厨师很有名。
column5: 這家餐廳的廚師很有名。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de chúshī hěn yǒumíng.
column7: The chef of this restaurant is famous.

column3: Red bean, the azuki bean, sweetened and used in desserts: 紅豆湯 "sweet red bean soup", 紅豆餅, 紅豆麵包. In poems 紅豆 also stands for longing. 豆 began as a picture of a serving dish on a stand, and was later borrowed for "bean".
column7: This bread has red bean inside.

column3: Hot water: 熱 "hot" + 水 "water". 熱水器 is a water heater, and 洗熱水澡 "take a hot bath". In Taiwan cafés and homes, drinking plain warm or hot water, 熱水, is common. Ask for 一杯熱水. 熱 has 灬 "fire" at the bottom.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi rèshuǐ.
column7: Please give me a cup of hot water.

column3: Enjoy (your food), said by the server or host when food is served: 請慢用. It literally says "take your time and use it". The guest might answer 謝謝. Used also for tea and snacks.
column7: Here is your food, please enjoy.

column3: To explode, blow up: 炸彈 "bomb", 爆炸 "explode", 氣球炸了 "the balloon burst". Informally also "to flare up in anger". This is the same character as 炸 "deep-fry", which is read zhá; the reading separates the two. 火 "fire" with 乍 "suddenly": a sudden flame.
column7: The balloon burst.

column3: Belt, of leather: 皮 "leather, skin" + 帶 "belt, strap". You wear it with 繫 or 戴: 繫皮帶. The character 帶 began as a picture of a woven belt, and it also means "to carry": 帶錢.
column6: Tā de pídài shì hēisè de.
column7: His belt is black.

column3: Cosmetics, makeup products: 化妝 "put on makeup" + 品 "goods". Shops that sell them are 化妝品店, and in Taiwan drugstores also stock them. 品 is three mouths, meaning "many kinds of things", as in 食品 "food products" and 用品 "supplies".
column6: Tā mǎi le hěn duō huàzhuāngpǐn.
column7: She bought a lot of cosmetics.

column3: Perfume: 香 "fragrant" + 水 "liquid". You wear it with 噴 "spray": 噴香水. Counted with 瓶. 香 is made of 禾 "grain" and 日, and it is the same 香 as in 香蕉 "banana" and 香港.
column7: This perfume smells nice.

column3: Wardrobe, closet: 衣 "clothes" + 櫃 "cabinet". Counted with 個: 一個衣櫃. For a built-in closet, 衣櫥 is also used. Clothes go "in the wardrobe": 衣服在衣櫃裡.
column7: All the clothes are in the wardrobe.

column3: In vain, for nothing, to no purpose: 白白浪費 "waste for nothing", 白白等了很久 "waited for nothing". It goes before a verb and says the effort had no result. It can also mean "white": 白白的. 白 alone means "white" and "in vain" too: 白跑一趟 "make a trip for nothing".
column6: Wǒ báibái děng le liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
column7: I waited two hours for nothing.

column3: Handsome, for a man, with a sense of good looks and spirit: 英俊的男生. 帥 is the casual word in Taiwan: 很帥. Women are 漂亮 or 美. 英 means "outstanding" and 俊 "good-looking".
column7: He is tall and handsome.

column3: Shoulder: 肩膀 is the spoken word, 肩 the single-character form. Combined with 寬 "wide", 痠 "sore", or the action 拍肩膀 "pat on the shoulder". 膀 has ⺼ "flesh" and 旁 for the sound (páng and bǎng).
column7: His shoulders are broad.

column3: Teeth: 牙 "tooth" + 齒 "tooth". 牙齒 is the full word, and in speech 牙 is often alone: 刷牙 "brush teeth", 牙醫 "dentist". 齒 shows a mouth full of teeth, and 止 was later added as a sound part.
column7: His teeth are very white.

column3: Blood. The character has two readings: xuè in compounds and formal words (血液, 貧血), and xiě in spoken use (吐血, 一滴血). The reading listed here is the spoken xiě. 皿 is a dish, and the stroke in it a drop: a drop of blood in a vessel.
column7: I don't dare look at blood.

column3: Brain, and "mind". It is most often met in 電腦 "computer", literally "electric brain", and in 頭腦 "mind" and 大腦 "brain". ⺼ "flesh" is the body-part sign, and the right side shows hair over the soft spot of the skull.
column7: My computer is broken.

column3: To bleed: 流 "flow" + 血 "blood". A verb with its object: 流了很多血 "bled a lot", 流血了 "is bleeding". Also used in a larger sense, for fighting that causes injuries: 流血衝突.
column7: Your finger is bleeding.

column3: To have diarrhea, spoken and not rude: 我拉肚子 "I have diarrhea", 拉了三次肚子. The pieces are 拉 "pull" and 肚子 "belly". It is a verb with its object and can be split. The doctor will ask 你拉肚子多久了？
column4: 我吃坏了东西，一直拉肚子。
column5: 我吃壞了東西，一直拉肚子。
column6: Wǒ chī huài le dōngxi, yīzhí lādùzi.
column7: I ate something bad and keep having diarrhea.

column3: Illegal drugs, narcotics: 毒 "poison" + 品 "goods". A narcotics case is 毒品案, and a dealer 毒販. 毒 means poison in general and has a plant on top. 品 is three mouths, "many things".
column6: Dúpǐn duì shēntǐ hěn bù hǎo.
column7: Drugs are very bad for the body.

column3: To take drugs, literally "inhale poison": 吸毒 is illegal in Taiwan. 吸 is "breathe in", and the mouth 口 on the left says it is done with the mouth, as in 吸菸 "smoke". 毒 "poison".
column7: Taking drugs is against the law.

column3: Traffic accident: 車 "vehicle" + 禍 "disaster". 發生車禍 "have an accident", 出車禍. 禍 has 礻 "spirit, altar" on the left, as a bad omen does, and 咼 for the sound.
column7: There was a traffic accident on the road yesterday.

column3: Life, and "fate" or "order": 生命 "life", 救命 "save a life", 命運 "fate", 一條命 "a life". 命 is counted with 條. The upper part 令 means "order" and the 口 "mouth" gives it, which is where "command" comes from.
column6: Yīshēng jiù le tā de mìng.
column7: The doctor saved his life.

column3: To wake up: 我六點就醒來了. 醒 is "to be awake" and 來 shows the coming of the new state. It is not the same as 起床 "get out of bed". 醒 has 酉 "wine jar" and 星 for the sound (xīng and xǐng).
column6: Wǒ jīntiān liù diǎn jiù xǐnglái le.
column7: I woke up at six today.

column3: Read zhuó, 著 is a written verb, "to wear" or "to put to, apply": 著裝 "attire", 穿著 "clothing", 著手 "set about", 著陸 "land (of a plane)". It is met mostly in compounds and formal writing. The same character is the particle zhe (坐著 "sitting") and zháo in 睡著 "fall asleep". Taiwan writes 著 for all of them; the mainland writes 着.
column6: Tā shēn zhuó hēisè xīzhuāng chūxí.
column7: He attended wearing a black suit.

column3: To dream, also in the figurative sense of wishful thinking: 你在作夢嗎？ "are you dreaming?", 別作夢了 "stop dreaming". Taiwan writes it 做夢 as often as 作夢. It is a verb with its object and can be split: 作了一個夢 "had a dream".
column7: Stop dreaming!

column3: Two meanings. "Morning and evening": 早晚各一次 "once in the morning and once in the evening". And "sooner or later": 他早晚會明白的. In the second meaning it goes before the verb, often with 會 or 都. 早 "early" + 晚 "late".
column7: He will understand sooner or later.

column3: To live one's life, to get by, of everyday life and its ups and downs, often of a couple or family: 好好過日子 "live a good life", 窮日子也要過. 過 "pass" + 日子 "days". It can imply living carefully with money.
column7: Let's live our lives well together.

column3: An apartment building. In Taiwan 公寓 usually means an older, low building of four or five floors without an elevator, as against 大樓 for a tall modern one with an elevator. A single apartment is 一戶. 寓 has 宀 "roof" for the meaning and 禺 for the sound (yù).
column4: 我住在一栋公寓的三楼。
column5: 我住在一棟公寓的三樓。
column6: Wǒ zhù zài yī dòng gōngyù de sān lóu.
column7: I live on the third floor of an apartment building.

column3: Tenant, lodger, the person who rents a room or apartment: 房 "room" + 客 "guest". The landlord is 房東 "house owner", and 房租 is the rent. 客 has 宀 "roof" with 各 under it, a guest under one's roof.
column6: Zhè jiān fángzi yǒu sān ge fángkè.
column7: This house has three tenants.

column3: Floor of a room, the surface you walk on, whether wood, tile or carpet. Typical verbs are 拖地板 "mop the floor" and 掃地板 "sweep the floor"; for a floor of a building (the second floor) say 樓 instead. 地 "ground" + 板 "board": 板 has 木 "wood" for its meaning and 反 for its sound.
column7: The floor is very clean.

column3: Toilet bowl, the fixture itself: 馬桶蓋 is the seat, and 沖馬桶 is "flush the toilet". The dictionary's older meaning, a wooden chamber pot, explains the odd look of 馬 "horse" here; 桶 "bucket, barrel" has 木 "wood" in it. For the room itself, say 廁所 or 洗手間.
column6: Mǎtǒng huài le, qǐng zhǎo rén lái xiū.
column7: The toilet is broken, please get someone to fix it.

column3: Endless, boundless, a written-style word, often in a four-character phrase: 樂趣無窮 "endless fun", 後患無窮 "endless trouble later". It goes after its noun as a predicate (not before it as 無窮的 plus noun, as often). 無 "without" + 窮 "end, to the limit"; 窮 also means "poor", and has 穴 "cave" on top.
column7: The fun of this game is endless.

column3: Like this, in this way, the spoken, slightly longer form of 這樣. It stands before a verb or alone as a reply: 這樣子不行 "this won't work", 你怎麼這樣子？ "why are you like this?" 樣子 means "appearance, shape", so 這樣子 is literally "this appearance"; 樣 has 木 "wood" in it, and 羕 for its sound.
column7: Don't talk like that.

column3: Almost, nearly, for something bad or unwanted that did not happen: 我差點遲到 "I was almost late" (and I wasn't). It goes before the verb. 差點沒 plus an unwanted event means the same thing: 差點沒摔倒 also "nearly fell". 差 here is read chà "lacking" (a different reading from chā "difference"), and 點 is "a little".
column4: 我差点忘了今天有考试。
column5: 我差點忘了今天有考試。
column6: Wǒ chàdiǎn wàng le jīntiān yǒu kǎoshì.
column7: I almost forgot that there is an exam today.

column3: Properly, well, carefully, used before a verb to urge someone to do it thoroughly: 好好休息 "get a good rest", 好好學 "study hard". The dictionary's form with 兒 is northern; in Taiwan people say 好好 and usually write 好好的 or 好好地. The second 好 is read in the first tone when the 兒 is added.
column7: You must get a good rest.

column3: Insect, bug, worm. 蟲 is three 虫 piled up, which is a picture of many small creatures; the form 虫 alone is a single one and is the part found in the names of many creatures (螞蟻, 蟲). In Taiwan the spoken word is 蟲子, and a person can be called 蟲 for a habit: 書蟲 "bookworm".
column6: Huāyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō chóng.
column7: There are many bugs in the garden.

column3: Ant. Both characters have 虫 "insect" for their meaning; 馬 and 義 give the sounds, and 馬 still sounds alike. The measure word is 隻: 一隻螞蟻. A saying is 螞蟻搬家 "ants moving house", taken as a sign that rain is coming.
column7: There are a lot of ants on the table.

column3: Lion, found only in compounds: 獅子, 雄獅 "male lion", 獅子座 "Leo", 海獅 "sea lion". 犭 "animal" is the meaning part, and 師 "teacher" the sound part, which still sounds the same (shī). Use 獅子 for "a lion" when it stands alone.
column7: This male lion is very big.

column3: Lion. The measure word is 隻: 一隻獅子. 獅子座 is the zodiac sign Leo, and temples in Taiwan have a pair of stone lions at the gate, 石獅. 獅 has 犭 for "animal" and 師 for the sound; the 子 is a neutral-tone suffix.
column6: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu liǎng zhī shīzi.
column7: There are two lions in the zoo.

column3: Rabbit, hare. The measure word is 隻: 一隻兔子; 小白兔 is the "little white rabbit" of children's songs, and 兔年 is the year of the rabbit in the zodiac. 兔 began as a picture of a rabbit; the 丶 at the bottom right is its tail.
column7: Rabbits like to eat carrots.

column3: Duck, seen mostly in compounds: 鴨子, 烤鴨 "roast duck" (Peking duck), 鴨肉 "duck meat", 北京烤鴨. 鳥 "bird" is the meaning part; 甲 was once the sound but no longer sounds like yā. The measure word is 隻.
column7: I want to eat roast duck.

column3: Tiger. 老 is a prefix here, as in 老鼠 "mouse" and has nothing to do with age. The measure word is 隻: 一隻老虎. 紙老虎 "paper tiger" means someone who only looks fierce. 虎 started as a picture of a tiger, and its top part 虍 is the head.
column6: Lǎohǔ bǐ māo dà hěn duō.
column7: A tiger is much bigger than a cat.

column3: Giant panda, literally "bear cat". In Taiwan 貓熊 "cat bear" is also used, but 熊貓 is the form the dictionary and most books give. 熊 is "bear"; 貓 "cat" has 豸 for the animal and 苗 for the sound (miáo, close to māo). The Taipei Zoo is known for its pandas.
column7: The Taipei Zoo has pandas.

column3: Trees taken together, with the feel of written Chinese: 保護樹木 "protect trees", 樹木茂盛 "the trees are lush". A single tree is 樹 with the measure word 棵: 一棵樹; 樹木 is not counted that way. Both characters have 木 "wood, tree"; in 樹 it is the meaning part and 尌 gives the sound.
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō shùmù.
column7: There are many trees in the park.

column3: Island. It goes with the measure word 座 for a named or large one: 那座島, and it is a part of many names: 小島, 島嶼, 半島 "peninsula", 離島 "outlying island". 島 is a mountain 山 with a bird 鳥 on it; the bird also gives the sound, which is close.
column6: Wǒmen zuò chuán qù nà zuò dǎo.
column7: We take a boat to that island.

column3: Ocean, the sea as a whole, in a general or scientific sense: 海洋生物 "marine life", 海洋污染 "ocean pollution", 保護海洋. For going to the sea, people say 海 or 海邊, not 海洋. Both characters have 氵 "water" for the meaning, and 洋 sounds the same as its part 羊 (yáng).
column6: Hǎiyáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō yú.
column7: There are many fish in the ocean.

column3: Beach. Taiwan also says 沙灘 "sand beach" and 海邊 "seaside". You go there to 玩 or 曬太陽: 去海灘玩 "go to the beach". 灘 is 氵 "water" with 難 for the sound (nán, now tān); the same part is in 攤 in 地攤.
column7: We go to the beach on weekends.

column3: Field, land for growing crops, especially a rice paddy: 稻田 "rice field", 田裡 "in the field", 田地. The character is a picture of a field divided into plots. It is also a common surname, and the same shape is part of many characters, such as 男 and 界.
column7: Grandpa works in the field.

column3: Two main uses. For wind: 刮風 "the wind blows", 刮大風 "a strong wind blows", 刮颱風 "a typhoon hits". And "to scrape, to shave": 刮鬍子 "shave (one's beard)". The knife 刂 on the right is the meaning part, which fits scraping.
column7: It is very windy outside today.

column3: Sunrise. 看日出 "watch the sunrise" is an activity people plan, such as on Alishan or Hehuanshan; its opposite is 日落 "sunset". 日 "sun" + 出 "come out"; 出 is a sprout over a container, growing out. In a sentence, use it with 看, or for time: 日出之前.
column4: 我们早上五点去看日出。
column5: 我們早上五點去看日出。
column6: Wǒmen zǎoshang wǔ diǎn qù kàn rìchū.
column7: We go to watch the sunrise at five in the morning.

column3: Gold, the metal as a thing, in spoken Chinese: 一塊金子 "a piece of gold". 黃金 is the more usual word for gold as a material or in the market, and 金 alone is used in compounds like 金牌 "gold medal" and 金錢 "money". The neutral-tone 子 is a suffix.
column6: Tā zài shān lǐ zhǎodào le jīnzi.
column7: He found gold in the mountains.

column3: Wood, tree, in compounds mostly: 木頭 "wood, timber", 樹木 "trees", 木板 "board". It is also a shape: a trunk with branches above and roots below. The same 木 is in 樹, 桌, 板 and 桶 as the meaning part, so it tells you a tree or something made of wood. 木 can also mean "numb".
column6: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì mùtou zuò de.
column7: This table is made of wood.

column3: Stone, rock, mostly in compounds: 石頭 "stone", 寶石 "gem", 石油 "petroleum", 石像 "stone statue". The shape is a stone 口 under a cliff 厂.
column6: Hébiān yǒu hěn duō dà shítou.
column7: There are many big stones by the river.

column3: City, metropolis, written-style: 大都市 "big city", 都市生活 "city life", 都市人. The 都 here is dū, not dōu "all"; the 阝 on its right is the city sign. In everyday speech people say 城市 for "city"; 都市 stresses a large, busy modern one, and works as a modifier before a noun.
column6: Dūshì de shēnghuó jiézòu hěn kuài.
column7: The pace of life in the city is fast.

column3: Geography, as a school subject or a place's features: 地理課 "geography class", 地理位置 "geographical location". 地 "earth" + 理 "order, principle". 理 has 王 "jade" in it for the meaning and 里 for the sound; it first meant working jade along its grain.
column6: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan shàng dìlǐ kè.
column7: I like geography class the most.

column3: Literally "under heaven": the whole world, or all of China in old texts. In modern Taiwan it is mostly in sayings and in names: 天下沒有白吃的午餐 "there is no such thing as a free lunch", 天下太平 "peace in the world", and a magazine called 天下. 天 is a person 大 with a line above, the sky over a man.
column6: Tiānxià méiyǒu bái chī de wǔcān.
column7: There is no such thing as a free lunch.

column3: Auditorium, assembly hall, the large room in a school, company or government building where meetings and ceremonies are held: 大禮堂, 在禮堂開會 "hold a meeting in the hall". 禮 "rite" + 堂 "hall"; 禮 has 礻 "altar" for the meaning, and 堂 has 土 "earth" with 尚 for the sound.
column7: The graduation ceremony is held in the auditorium.

column3: Street stall with goods laid out on the ground or on a cloth: 擺地攤 "set up a stall", 地攤貨 "cheap goods from a street stall". In Taiwan, the stalls of a night market are 攤販 or 攤位 instead. 攤 has 扌 "hand" for the meaning, since you spread things out, and 難 for the sound.
column4: 他在夜市摆地摊卖衣服。
column5: 他在夜市擺地攤賣衣服。
column6: Tā zài yèshì bǎi dìtān mài yīfu.
column7: He sets up a street stall at the night market and sells clothes.

column3: Meeting place, venue, the place where a conference or event is held: 會場在哪裡？ "where is the venue?", 進入會場 "enter the hall". 會 "meet" + 場 "place". 場 here is read chǎng, as in 市場 and 操場. Not used for the room of a small meeting; for that, say 會議室.
column7: The venue is on the second floor.

column3: Go out into the streets. In Taiwan it is mostly used for going out to do an errand, as in 上街買菜 "go out to buy groceries", or for taking to the streets in a protest: 上街抗議. For strolling and shopping for fun, 逛街 is the usual word. 街 "street" has 行 around 圭, which gives the sound.
column7: Mom went out to buy groceries.

column3: A "tram" or electric train that runs on rails. In Taiwan you meet it mostly when people talk about Japan's trains and trams; for Taipei's metro the word is 捷運, and an electric car is 電動車. 電 "electric, lightning" has 雨 "rain" on top, as lightning comes with storms; 車 "vehicle" is a picture of a cart seen from above.
column7: Japan's trains are very punctual.

column3: Truck, lorry. 卡車 is the standard word, with 貨車 "goods vehicle" as another common one; a big one is 大卡車, and the measure word is 輛: 一輛卡車. The 卡 is a sound borrowed from a foreign word, and is also in 卡片 "card" and 卡通 "cartoon".
column6: Yī liàng dà kǎchē tíng zài lùbiān.
column7: A big truck is parked by the roadside.

column3: Traffic light, literally "red-green light". 等紅燈 "wait for the red light", 闖紅燈 "run a red light", 過紅綠燈 "go past the traffic light"; directions often use it: 到紅綠燈右轉 "turn right at the light". 紅 and 綠 both have the silk sign 糸, a color word; 工 in 紅 still sounds like hóng, and 彔 in 綠 (lù) gives lǜ.
column7: There is a traffic light up ahead.

column3: Tire. 換輪胎 "change a tire", 爆胎 "a blowout", and 輪胎沒氣了 "the tire is flat". 輪 "wheel" has 車 on the left and 侖 for the sound. 胎 has ⺼ "flesh" and 台 for the sound, and on its own means "fetus, unborn child".
column6: Jiǎotàchē de lúntāi méi qì le.
column7: The bicycle's tire is flat.

column3: Get lost, lose one's way, a verb with its object built in: 我迷路了, 迷了路 "got lost", 在山上迷路. It is not used with a place as object (not 迷路台北; say 在台北迷路). 迷 has 辶 "walk" with 米 as the sound, and 路 has 足 "foot" with 各 for the sound.
column7: I got lost in Taipei.

column3: Two uses. "Catch" a vehicle or a deadline: 趕上最後一班車 "catch the last bus", and 趕不上 "can't make it in time". And "catch up with": 他很快就趕上了大家 "he soon caught up with everyone". 趕 has 走 "run" as its meaning part and 旱 for the sound (hàn, now gǎn).
column4: 我赶上了最后一班捷运。
column5: 我趕上了最後一班捷運。
column6: Wǒ gǎnshàng le zuìhòu yī bān jiéyùn.
column7: I caught the last metro train.

column3: Be at a distance from, used as a verb in a more formal style, with a place or a time: 距車站不遠 "not far from the station", 距今三年 "three years from now". In ordinary speech the distance word is 距離 or 離. 足 "foot" is the meaning part and 巨 the sound; both are read jù.
column7: The school is not far from the station.

column3: Scheduled flight, a particular flight on the timetable: 班機延誤 "the flight is delayed", 下一班班機 "the next flight". 班 is a scheduled run (as in 班車 "bus service"), and 機 is "aircraft" (in 飛機). 班機 is the written or announced form; 航班 means the same.
column7: Our flight is delayed.

column3: Arrive at, reach a destination, formal: used in announcements, news and schedules, 抵達機場 "arrive at the airport", 準時抵達. In speech, 到 is the normal word. It takes the place directly, with no 到 before it. 達 has 辶 "walk" for its meaning; 抵 has 扌 "hand" and 氐 for the sound.
column4: 飞机将在十点抵达台北。
column5: 飛機將在十點抵達台北。
column6: Fēijī jiāng zài shí diǎn dǐdá Táiběi.
column7: The plane will arrive in Taipei at ten o'clock.

column3: The same day, the day that something happens: 當天來回 "go and come back the same day", 當天的報紙 "that day's paper", 活動當天 "on the day of the event". Read dàng, as in 當時 "at that time"; it points to a day just mentioned or fixed, not to "today", which is 今天.
column7: We came back the same day.

column3: Year after year, every year. Doubling a measure-like word gives "every": 天天, 人人, 年年. It usually comes with 都 before the verb: 年年都去 "go every year". It is also in the New Year wish 年年有餘 "may there be a surplus every year". 年 once showed a man carrying grain, the yearly harvest.
column6: Tā niánnián dōu huí lǎojiā guònián.
column7: Every year he goes back to his hometown for the New Year.

column3: Every day. It goes before the verb, usually with 都: 天天都運動 "exercise every day"; 每天 means the same and is a bit more neutral. Doubling a character gives "every" in 天天, 年年, 人人. 天 is the sky 一 over a person 大.
column7: I walk to work every day.

column3: A lifetime, the whole of one's life, never alone but with a number or a pointing word: 一輩子 "all one's life", 這輩子 "in this life", 下輩子 "next life". 輩 originally means a generation. The 子 is neutral, so bèizi.
column6: Wǒ zhè bèizi dōu bù huì wàngjì.
column7: I will never forget it as long as I live.

column3: For the moment, for a short while: 一時想不起來 "can't recall it for the moment", 一時衝動 "on an impulse", 一時之間 "for a moment". It points to a short and passing state, not to a stretch of time you can measure; for that use 一會兒. 時 has 日 "sun, day" for its meaning and 寺 for the sound.
column4: 我一时想不起来他的名字。
column5: 我一時想不起來他的名字。
column6: Wǒ yīshí xiǎng bù qǐlái tā de míngzi.
column7: I can't recall his name for the moment.

column3: Soon, at an early date, said about something hoped for: 祝你早日康復 "I hope you recover soon", 早日完成 "complete it soon", 早日見面. It is formal and used in wishes and plans, not for a time that is already fixed. 早 is a sun 日 at the top of a ten-like shape, the sun just risen.
column7: I hope you recover soon.

column3: Another day, some other time, for putting something off: 改天再聊 "let's talk another day", 改天見. It is a polite way to say not today, and it is sometimes just a polite way of not setting a date at all. 改 is "to change": 改天 is "change the day".
column6: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu shì, gǎitiān zài yuē.
column7: I have something on today, let's meet another day.

column3: Historic site, ancient monument. In Taiwan 古蹟 is also an official category of protected sites, and the word is written 古蹟 there: 名勝古蹟 "famous sights and historic sites", 參觀古蹟. 蹟 has 足 "foot" for the meaning, since it is a trace left behind, and 責 for the sound. 古 is ten 十 mouths 口, words handed down by many.
column7: Tainan has many historic sites.

column3: Suddenly or "to overlook", mostly in compounds: 忽然, 忽略 "overlook", 忽視. Alone it appears in a pair in written style: 忽冷忽熱 "now cold, now hot", 忽高忽低 "now high, now low". 心 "heart" is the meaning part, which fits a lapse of attention; 勿 gives a distant sound.
column7: The weather is now cold, now hot.

column3: In a row, in succession. It goes before a number and a measure and a verb: 一連三天 "three days in a row", 一連說了三次 "said it three times in a row". 連 has 辶 "move" and 車 "cart", a row of carts one after another, and also gives 連續 "continuous" and 連接 "connect".
column6: Tā yīlián sān tiān méi shuìjiào.
column7: He did not sleep for three days in a row.

column3: Never, for a habit or a rule: 他從不喝酒 "he never drinks", 我從不遲到. It says "does not, ever" about what someone regularly does. For "has never done it" in one's experience, use 從來沒有 instead. 從 has 彳 "step" with two people following each other.
column7: He never drinks.

column3: A measure word for things on a string or in a bunch: 一串鑰匙 "a bunch of keys", 一串葡萄 "a bunch of grapes", 一串珍珠. As a verb it means "to string together" or "to skewer": 串起來. The shape is two 口 threaded on a stick 丨. 肉串 and 烤肉串 are skewers.
column6: Tā mǎi le yī chuàn pútáo.
column7: He bought a bunch of grapes.

column3: A measure word for class periods: 一堂課 "one class", 這堂課, 上完一堂課. It also means "hall", as in 教堂 "church" and 禮堂 "auditorium". 土 "earth" is the meaning part, a raised hall, and 尚 gives the sound, which has stayed close (shàng, táng).
column6: Zhè táng kè hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: This class is very interesting.

column3: Meter, the unit of length. 公尺 is the official name in Taiwan, while 米 is used in speech and the mainland: 一百公尺 "100 meters". 公里 is "kilometer", 公分 "centimeter", 公斤 "kilogram". The 公 means "public, metric", and 尺 was the old foot-length unit.
column4: 这栋大楼有两百公尺高。
column5: 這棟大樓有兩百公尺高。
column6: Zhè dòng dàlóu yǒu liǎng bǎi gōngchǐ gāo.
column7: This building is two hundred meters tall.

column3: Centimeter in Taiwan: 一百七十公分 "170 cm" is how height is given. The dictionary also records an old meaning, "gram"; ignore that, since a gram is 公克. 公 "metric" + 分 "a hundredth part"; 公尺 is the meter, and a centimeter is a hundredth of one.
column6: Tā yī bǎi bāshí gōngfēn gāo.
column7: He is 180 centimeters tall.

column3: Gram. 公克 is the full formal name; in speech and on food labels it is often just 克: 五百公克 "500 grams". 公斤 is "kilogram" (1000 公克). The 克 alone is often attached to a number. The 公 is the same metric prefix as in 公尺 and 公分.
column6: Zhè bāo táng yǒu wǔ bǎi gōngkè.
column7: This bag of sugar weighs five hundred grams.

column3: Ping, Taiwan's unit of floor area, about 3.3 square meters: 三十坪的房子 "a 30-ping home". Housing is sold and rented by it, with prices 每坪. The character is 土 "earth" + 平 "flat", which also gives the sound.
column6: Zhè jiān gōngyù yǒu sānshí píng.
column7: This apartment is thirty ping.

column3: To force, to press: 逼 plus a person plus a verb, 不要逼我做 "don't force me to do", 逼他說實話. It stresses pressure against the person's will. Also 逼近 "close in on". 辶 "move" is the meaning part, which fits pushing someone along; 畐 gives the sound.
column4: 不要逼我做不想做的事。
column5: 不要逼我做不想做的事。
column6: Bùyào bī wǒ zuò bù xiǎng zuò de shì.
column7: Don't force me to do things I don't want to do.

column3: Run into, come across, by chance, a person, a situation or luck: 碰上老朋友, 碰上下雨 "get caught in the rain", 碰上塞車. 碰到 means almost the same and is as common. 碰 "bump" has 石 "stone" for its meaning (hitting a hard thing) and 並 for the sound.
column4: 我在路上碰上了老同学。
column5: 我在路上碰上了老同學。
column6: Wǒ zài lùshang pèngshàng le lǎo tóngxué.
column7: I ran into an old classmate on the way.

column3: Save money, a verb with its object: 省錢, 省了不少錢 "saved quite a lot of money". It also works as an adjective, "economical": 這個方法很省錢. 省 is read shěng here "to save" (also xǐng "to reflect"). 錢 has 釒 "metal" for money and 戔 as its sound.
column7: Cooking for yourself saves more money.

column3: Give change, what the cashier does: 找您五十元 "here is 50 yuan change for you", 不用找錢了 "keep the change". Taiwan also says 找零. The other sense, "look for money" (find funding) belongs to business talk. 找 has 扌 "hand" for the meaning and 戈 "spear"; it is the same 找 as "look for".
column7: Keep the change.

column3: Bargain, haggle over the price, at night markets, traditional markets and small shops: 可以講價嗎？ "can I bargain?" In Taiwan 殺價 is also common for "knock down the price", and a firm price is 不二價. 價 "price" has 亻 "person" and 賈, a word for merchant that also gives the sound (jià, gǔ).
column7: You can bargain at the night market.

column3: Shop sign, the board over the door, and also the "reputation" of a business: 砸招牌 "ruin the name". 招牌菜 is a restaurant's "signature dish", which you will see on many Taiwanese menus. 招 has 扌 "hand", beckoning, with 召 for the sound; 牌 is 片 "slab" with 卑 for the sound. The 牌 is neutral here.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de zhāopai hěn dà.
column7: This shop's sign is very big.

column3: Poster, the kind put up for a film, concert or event: 電影海報 "film poster", 貼海報 "put up a poster". The measure word is 張: 一張海報. 報 means "to report, to announce" and 海 here just suggests something large and seen by many. For a newspaper, 報紙.
column4: 墙上贴着一张电影海报。
column5: 牆上貼著一張電影海報。
column6: Qiáng shàng tiēzhe yī zhāng diànyǐng hǎibào.
column7: There is a movie poster on the wall.

column3: Articles, supplies for a certain use. It follows the kind of use: 日常用品 "daily necessities", 辦公用品 "office supplies", 運動用品 "sports goods", 學生用品. It is a collective word and not counted by itself. 品 is three 口 together, "many objects".
column6: Zhè jiā diàn mài rìcháng yòngpǐn.
column7: This shop sells daily necessities.

column3: Be fooled, be taken in by a trick or false advertisement: 我上當了 "I've been had", 小心別上當 "be careful not to be fooled", 上了他的當. The 當 is read dàng here, not dāng. The person who is cheated is the subject; the swindler comes after 被 or 了.
column4: 我上当了，这个东西是假的。
column5: 我上當了，這個東西是假的。
column6: Wǒ shàngdàng le, zhège dōngxi shì jiǎ de.
column7: I was fooled, this thing is fake.

column3: Everyone, everybody. The doubled character means "every": 人人都 plus the verb: 人人都知道 "everyone knows". It can be the subject of a proverb: 人人有責 "everyone has a duty". 人 is a picture of a standing person seen from the side.
column7: Everyone likes him.

column3: More or less, to some extent, for a small but real amount: 多多少少知道一些 "know a little", 多多少少有關係. It is a spoken adverb, placed before the verb. It is not the same as 多少 "how many". 多 is two evening signs 夕 piled up, "many".
column7: He knows something about it, more or less.

column3: Every kind, all kinds of things: 樣樣都好 "everything is good", 樣樣都會 "can do everything", 樣樣齊全 "everything is there". The doubled 樣 is a measure for "kinds", and it is followed by 都 or 俱. 樣 has 木 "wood" in it and 羕 as its sound.
column7: She can do everything.

column3: All kinds of, a variety of: it goes before a noun, with 的: 各式各樣的人 "all kinds of people", 各式各樣的商品. A four-character phrase: 各 "each" + 式 "style" + 各 + 樣 "kind". In writing it is also 各式各樣. It does not take 都 after it, because it modifies the noun.
column4: 夜市里有各式各样的小吃。
column5: 夜市裡有各式各樣的小吃。
column6: Yèshì lǐ yǒu gèshìgèyàng de xiǎochī.
column7: There are all kinds of snacks at the night market.

column3: At most, a maximum of, before the number: 最多十個 "at most ten", 最多只能 "can only at most". It sets an upper limit. The opposite is 最少 "at least". 最多 can also mean "the most", as in 最多人 "the most people". 最 is read zuì: "most".
column6: Wǒ zuìduō zhǐ néng děng shí fēnzhōng.
column7: I can wait ten minutes at most.

column3: The polite way to ask someone's surname: 請問您貴姓？ "may I ask your surname?" The answer is 我姓王, not 我貴姓王; 貴 "honorable" is only for the other person. 免貴姓王 is the humble reply. 姓 has 女 "woman" and 生 "give birth"; surnames once came through the mother.
column7: May I ask your surname?

column3: Say hello to, send regards to: 向你的家人問好 "give my regards to your family", 替我向他問好 "say hi to him for me". It takes 向 or 替 for the person. 問 "ask" has 口 "mouth" inside the gate 門, which gives the sound; 好 is 女 "woman" + 子 "child".
column6: Qǐng tì wǒ xiàng nǐ fùmǔ wènhǎo.
column7: Please give my regards to your parents.

column3: Apologize: 向他道歉 "apologize to him", 道歉信 "letter of apology". A verb and an object in one: 道 "say" + 歉 "regret", so you can also say 道了歉. It is a formal and real apology; the light one is 對不起. 歉 has 欠 "lack", and 兼 for the sound, which also gives 謙 in 謙虛.
column7: You should apologize to him.

column3: Thank, mostly in 謝謝 and compounds: 多謝 "many thanks", 感謝 "be grateful", 謝謝你. A flower can 謝 "wither" and a person 謝絕 "decline". 言 "speech" is the meaning part and 射 gives the sound (shè, now xiè).
column7: Many thanks for your help.

column3: Forgive, excuse: 請原諒我 "please forgive me", 原諒他 "forgive him". It takes the person as object and the fault after 的 or in a clause: 原諒我遲到. 原 is a spring bursting out of a cliff, "origin"; 諒 has 言 "speech" and 京, which no longer sounds alike.
column7: Please forgive me for being late.

column3: Unfamiliar, strange, for a place, face or thing that you do not know: 陌生人 "stranger", 對這裡很陌生 "unfamiliar with this place". Its opposite is 熟悉. 陌 has 阝 and 百; it was a path between fields, and the word is only used together with 生 "raw, unfamiliar".
column6: Wǒ duì zhège chéngshì hěn mòshēng.
column7: I am not familiar with this city.

column3: Considerate, thoughtful of others' needs: 他很體貼 "he is very considerate", 體貼的先生 "a considerate husband". It describes a person who senses what you need; it can also be a verb, 體貼別人. 體 "body" + 貼 "stick close": the second character has 貝 "shell, money" and 占.
column7: He is very considerate toward his family.

column3: Gentle, soft-spoken, tender, for a person or a voice: 溫柔的聲音 "a gentle voice", 個性溫柔. Used more of women, but men can be 溫柔 too. 溫 has 氵 "water" for warmth; 柔 has 木 "wood" under 矛, a branch soft enough to bend.
column7: Her voice is very gentle.

column3: Conversation in the sense of spoken practice in a language class: 英語會話 "English conversation", 會話課, 基本會話. It is a school word, a skill rather than an everyday chat; for a chat, 聊天 or 談話. 會 means "meet" here; 話 is 言 "speech" and 舌 "tongue".
column4: 我每周上两堂中文会话课。
column5: 我每週上兩堂中文會話課。
column6: Wǒ měi zhōu shàng liǎng táng Zhōngwén huìhuà kè.
column7: I have two Chinese conversation classes a week.

column3: Contact, get in touch: 連絡你 "contact you", 保持連絡 "stay in touch", 連絡電話 "contact phone number". 聯絡 is a very common way to write it as well, and the two are used the same. Both characters belong together: 連 "link" and 絡 "net" (糸 "thread").
column7: Let's stay in touch.

column3: Exaggerated, a spoken word with a feeling of disbelief: 太誇張了 "that's over the top", 說得很誇張. It also describes anything extreme: 價格很誇張 "the price is outrageous". 誇 has 言 "speech" and 夸 as sound; 張 has 弓 "bow" and 長, which gives the sound. A bow stretched open is the sense of "to stretch".
column6: Nǐ shuō de tài kuāzhāng le.
column7: You are exaggerating too much.

column3: Well-behaved, obedient, said of children and pets: 這孩子很乖 "this child is well-behaved", 乖乖聽話 "be good and listen". Adults say it to a child warmly, as 乖. 乖乖 as a doubled form can also mean "obediently", and in speech can be a cry of surprise.
column7: This child is very well-behaved.

column3: Sensible, understanding, of a child who acts older than their age and understands what others need: 這孩子很懂事. It is a compliment to a young person; it is not used of adults in the same way. 懂 "understand" has 忄 "heart, mind", and 事 "matter" once showed a hand holding a flag.
column4: 她虽然年纪小，但很懂事。
column5: 她雖然年紀小，但很懂事。
column6: Tā suīrán niánjì xiǎo, dàn hěn dǒngshì.
column7: Although she is young, she is very sensible.

column3: Modest, humble, about how a person talks of themselves: 他很謙虛 "he is very modest", 謙虛地說 "say modestly". Saying 哪裡哪裡 or 不敢當 after a compliment is the polite and modest reply. 謙虛使人進步 "modesty helps one improve" is a saying. 謙 and 歉 share the part 兼 and the sound qiān/qiàn.
column4: 他很有才华，但是很谦虚。
column5: 他很有才華，但是很謙虛。
column6: Tā hěn yǒu cáihuá, dànshì hěn qiānxū.
column7: He is very talented, but also modest.

column3: Cheerful, outgoing, open of a person's character: 個性開朗 "a cheerful personality", 開朗的人. It means a bright and open nature, not just being happy today. The opposite is 內向 or 憂鬱. 開 "open" + 朗 "bright"; 朗 has 月 "moon" and 良, which gives the sound.
column7: She has a cheerful personality.

column3: Filial, good to one's parents and grandparents: 孝順父母 "be devoted to one's parents", 孝順的孩子. It is a true virtue in Chinese culture, taken seriously. 孝 is a child 子 under an old man 耂, carrying him; 順 means "smooth, obedient", with 頁 "head" and 川 "river" for the sound.
column7: He is very good to his parents.

column3: Careful, attentive to detail: 做事細心 "work carefully", 她很細心. It is a good quality of a person; for something done with care, say 仔細. The opposite is 粗心 "careless". 細 "thin, fine" has 糸 "thread" and 田; 心 is "heart".
column7: She is very careful in her work.

column3: Two senses. "Proud (of)", in a good way: 我為你感到驕傲 "I'm proud of you", 以…為驕傲. And "arrogant, conceited", in a bad way: 他太驕傲了. The context decides. 驕 has 馬 "horse" and 喬 for the sound (a proud horse); 傲 has 亻 "person" and 敖 for the sound.
column7: I feel proud of you.

column3: Muddled, confused, foolish: 他老糊塗了 "he has become muddled with age", 一時糊塗 "a moment of confusion", 裝糊塗 "pretend not to understand". It describes a mind that is unclear, not just a lack of knowledge. The second syllable is neutral: hútu. 糊 has 米 "rice" and is "paste"; it is read hú (or hù) when it means paste.
column6: Tā niánjì dà le, yǒudiǎn hútu.
column7: He is old now and a little muddled.

column3: Endure, put up with, exercise patience: 忍耐一下 "bear with it for a moment", 忍耐不住 "can't hold back". It is about holding back one's feelings or pain; 忍受 is "endure" something unpleasant. 忍 is a knife 刃 over a heart 心. 耐 means "to bear, to last", and is in 耐心 "patience" and 耐用 "durable".
column7: Please bear with it a little longer.

column3: Good at, one's specialty, especially a skill such as cooking: 拿手菜 "a signature dish", 拿手好戲 "a party piece". It is mostly an adjective after 很 or 最, and often with 對: 他對做菜很拿手. 拿 is 手 "hand" with 合 for the sound, and "hand" appears again in the second character, which gives a picture of having something well in hand.
column7: When it comes to cooking, I am best at it.

column3: Fierce, vicious: 那隻狗很兇 "that dog is fierce", 兇手 "murderer", 兇惡 "ferocious". It is also said of a person scolding, 她罵得很兇. Taiwan usually writes this 兇; the form 凶 is kept for "ominous, unlucky" in 吉凶 "good or bad luck". The short form is also what the mainland writes for both.
column7: That dog is fierce.

column3: Happy, pleasant, cheerful, a little formal and often in greetings and wishes: 祝你週末愉快 "have a nice weekend", 旅途愉快 "have a good trip", 心情愉快 "in a good mood". 快 alone also means "fast", but here it is "joyful". Both characters have 忄 "heart" for the meaning, with 俞 and 夬 for the sounds.
column7: Have a nice weekend!

column3: Comfortable, at ease, free: 一個人很自在 "very comfortable alone", 自由自在 "free and easy"; 不自在 is "ill at ease". It is about the feeling of being relaxed, without tension. The second 在 is neutral: zìzai. 自 is a picture of a nose, because people point to the nose for "me"; here it just means "self".
column6: Yī ge rén zhù hěn zìzai.
column7: Living alone is very comfortable.

column3: Feel at ease, set one's mind at rest: 請安心 "please don't worry", 讓人安心 "puts one at ease", 安心工作 "work without distractions". 安心 as a verb: 我安心了 "I can relax now". 安 is a woman 女 under a roof 宀, a symbol of safety; 心 is "heart".
column4: 听到你平安，我就安心了。
column5: 聽到你平安，我就安心了。
column6: Tīngdào nǐ píng'ān, wǒ jiù ānxīn le.
column7: When I heard you were safe, I felt at ease.

column3: Stable, settled: 生活安定 "a settled life", 安定的工作 "a steady job", 情緒安定 "emotionally stable", and as a verb 安定下來 "settle down". It also means to calm someone. The first character is "peace" and the second a person 疋 settled under a roof 宀. 穩定 is close, for the economy or prices.
column4: 他现在有了安定的工作。
column5: 他現在有了安定的工作。
column6: Tā xiànzài yǒu le āndìng de gōngzuò.
column7: He now has a steady job.

column3: Worry, trouble as a noun, and "to worry" as a verb: 有很多煩惱 "have many worries", 別煩惱了 "stop worrying", 煩惱的事. It is a mental trouble, more about feeling than about a plan. Both characters have a part for the mind: 煩 has 火 "fire" and 頁 "head", a hot head, and 惱 has 忄 "heart".
column6: Tā zuìjìn yǒu hěn duō fánnǎo.
column7: He has many worries recently.

column3: Wish one could (right now), "be itching to": 恨不得馬上回家 "can't wait to go home at once", 我恨不得飛過去. It expresses a strong wish for something that is not possible or not happening yet. It does not mean "hate"; the 恨 literally says "hate that one cannot". The 不 and 得 are neutral: hènbude.
column7: I can't wait to go home right now.

column3: Hateful, detestable, an angry exclamation or description: 可惡！ "damn it!", 真可惡 "how hateful", 可惡的小偷. 惡 is read wù "to hate" here, not è "evil". 可 "worthy of" + 惡 "hate", so it means "worth hating". 惡 has 心 "heart" at the bottom.
column7: This thief is really hateful!

column3: Get a fright, be startled, literally "scared for one jump": 嚇了一跳, 嚇我一跳 "gave me a start". The 了 and the person go inside it. It is said for a surprise as well as for fear. 嚇 has 口 "mouth" and 赫, and is read xià "frighten" here (hè in 恐嚇 is "threaten"); 跳 is "jump".
column4: 听到这个消息，我吓一跳。
column5: 聽到這個消息，我嚇一跳。
column7: When I heard the news, I was startled.

column3: Surprised, astonished at something unexpected, a little formal: 很驚訝, 感到驚訝, 令人驚訝. It is a milder word than 吃驚 and is for surprise, not for fear. 驚 has 馬 "horse", a horse startled, and 敬 for the sound; 訝 has 言 "speech" and 牙.
column7: Everyone is surprised.

column3: Lose one's temper, throw a tantrum: 對孩子發脾氣 "lose one's temper with the child", 不要發脾氣. The object of the anger is marked with 對 or 向. 發 "emit" + 脾氣 "temper": 脾 is the "spleen", which has 月 (⺼) "flesh" in it, traditionally linked with temper. 脾氣 alone is "temper": 好脾氣 "good-tempered".
column7: He often loses his temper with the children.

column3: Cold, indifferent, unenthusiastic: 態度冷淡 "a cool attitude", 反應冷淡 "a lukewarm response". It can also mean "slack" of business: 生意冷淡. It is about people's attitude and not about the weather, which is just 冷. 淡 has 氵 "water" and means "weak, light" in 淡茶 "weak tea" and 清淡 "light" in taste.
column6: Tā duì wǒ de tàidù hěn lěngdàn.
column7: His attitude toward me is very cold.

column3: Setback, frustration: 遇到挫折 "meet with a setback", 面對挫折 "face setbacks", 挫折感 "a feeling of frustration". It names the difficulty or failure itself, not the feeling alone. Both characters have 扌 "hand" in them, as things that break something: 挫 "to defeat" and 折 "to break", an axe 斤 in the hand.
column6: Tā yùdào cuòzhé yě bù fàngqì.
column7: Even when he meets setbacks, he does not give up.

column3: Otherwise, or else: 快一點，要不然會遲到 "hurry, or you'll be late". It comes at the start of a clause and gives the bad result of what was just said; it can also offer an alternative: 要不然我們坐捷運吧 "or else, let's take the metro". 要不然 is spoken; the shorter 不然 means the same.
column7: Hurry up, or you'll be late.

column3: If it were not for, "had it not been for": it begins a sentence about something that did not happen: 要不是你幫忙，我不可能完成 "without your help I could not have finished". It is followed by a person or a fact, and the result clause often has 早就 or 就. The neutral 不 makes it yàobushì.
column4: 要不是你帮忙，我不可能完成。
column5: 要不是你幫忙，我不可能完成。
column6: Yàobushì nǐ bāngmáng, wǒ bù kěnéng wánchéng.
column7: If it were not for your help, I could not have finished.

column3: Moreover, besides, what's more, adding a reason that is even stronger than the one before: 這家店很遠，況且今天下雨 "the shop is far, and besides it's raining". It goes at the start of the second clause, with a comma before. 況 has 氵 "water" and 兄 "elder brother" for the sound.
column4: 这家店很远，况且今天下雨。
column5: 這家店很遠，況且今天下雨。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn hěn yuǎn, kuàngqiě jīntiān xiàyǔ.
column7: This shop is far, and besides, it is raining today.

column3: Long for, look forward to, with hope and some impatience: 盼望你來 "hope you will come", 盼望已久 "long awaited", 盼望著暑假 "looking forward to the summer vacation". It is stronger and more emotional than 希望. 盼 has 目 "eye", looking, and 分 for the sound; 望 means to gaze at a distance, with 月 "moon".
column6: Wǒ pànwàng zhe shǔjià kuài diǎn dào.
column7: I am looking forward to the summer vacation arriving soon.

column3: Care about, mind, mostly in the negative: 我不在意 "I don't mind", 別太在意 "don't take it to heart", 很在意別人的看法 "care a lot about what others think". It is about attention given to something; it is not "be at" a place. 在 "be at" + 意 "mind, thoughts".
column6: Biérén zěnme shuō, wǒ bù zàiyì.
column7: I don't care what others say.

column3: Ski, skiing: 去滑雪 "go skiing", 滑雪場 "ski resort", 滑雪板 "ski, snowboard". Taiwan has little snow, so people usually go skiing abroad, in Japan or Korea. 滑 "slide" + 雪 "snow". 滑 has 氵 "water", a slippery surface, with 骨 as an old sound; 雪 has 雨 "rain" on top.
column7: I want to go skiing in Japan.

column3: Ball game, match, for team sports like baseball and basketball: 看球賽 "watch a game", 籃球賽, 棒球賽, 球賽結束 "the game is over". 比賽 is the general word for "a competition". 球 "ball" + 賽 "contest"; 賽 contains 貝 "shell, money", an old reference to prizes.
column7: Yesterday's game was very exciting.

column3: Player in a ball sport, a member of a team: 棒球員 is rare, so say 籃球員 or just 球員; 這位球員 "this player", 職業球員 "professional player". 員 is "member, person" and appears in 職員, 演員 and 學員. 球 has 王 as the jade sign and 求 for the sound.
column6: Zhè wèi qiúyuán pǎo de hěn kuài.
column7: This player runs very fast.

column3: Tease, amuse, make laugh: 逗孩子笑 "make a child laugh", 逗貓 "play with a cat", and in speech 很逗 "very funny". 逗號 is a "comma", the pause mark. 辶 "move" is the meaning part and 豆 the sound, and they still sound alike (dòu).
column6: Tā hěn huì dòu háizi xiào.
column7: He is good at making children laugh.

column3: Camping, staying outdoors in a tent: 去露營, 露營區 "campsite", 露營車 "camper van". It has become popular in Taiwan. 露 means "to expose, to be exposed", and also "dew"; here it is read lù, but in 露出 "show" it is lòu. 營 is a camp, as in 營地.
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù shān shàng lùyíng.
column7: On the weekend we go camping in the mountains.

column3: Plot, storyline of a film, a play or a TV drama: 劇情很精彩 "the plot is exciting", 劇情簡介 "synopsis". 劇 "drama" + 情 "situation, circumstances". 劇 has 刂 "knife", and 情 has 忄 "heart"; 青 gives its sound, which is close to qíng.
column4: 这部电影的剧情很感人。
column5: 這部電影的劇情很感人。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng de jùqíng hěn gǎnrén.
column7: The plot of this film is very moving.

column3: Ending, outcome of a story or an event: 好的結局 "a good ending", 快樂的結局 "a happy ending", 結局如何 "how does it end?", 悲慘的結局. It stresses how things turn out in the end. 結 is "to tie" with 糸 "thread"; 局 is a "round, state of affairs", as in 結局 "the final state".
column4: 这个故事的结局很意外。
column5: 這個故事的結局很意外。
column6: Zhège gùshi de jiéjú hěn yìwài.
column7: The ending of this story is unexpected.

column3: Singing star, a famous singer: 流行歌星 "pop star", 一位歌星. For a singer in general, 歌手 is the usual word in Taiwan, and 歌星 stresses fame. 星 is "star" with 日 "sun" on top and 生 for the sound (shēng, close to xīng). 歌 has 欠 "yawning mouth" in it.
column6: Tā shì yī wèi yǒumíng de gēxīng.
column7: She is a famous singer.

column3: Sing together, "chorus": 合唱一首歌 "sing a song together", 合唱團 "choir", 男女合唱. It is both a verb and a noun. 合 "together" + 唱 "sing"; 唱 has 口 "mouth" for the meaning and 昌, which still sounds like chāng.
column4: 他们一起合唱了一首歌。
column5: 他們一起合唱了一首歌。
column6: Tāmen yīqǐ héchàng le yī shǒu gē.
column7: They sang a song together.

column3: Band, orchestra, music ensemble: 管絃樂團 "orchestra", 搖滾樂團 "rock band", 國家樂團. It is the usual word for a pop or rock band in Taiwan. 樂 is read yuè "music" here, and lè in 快樂 "happy". The character shows an instrument with strings 幺 on a wooden frame 木. 團 is a group, enclosed in 囗.
column4: 这个乐团下个月来台湾表演。
column5: 這個樂團下個月來台灣表演。
column6: Zhège yuètuán xià ge yuè lái Táiwān biǎoyǎn.
column7: This band is coming to Taiwan to perform next month.

column3: Tone of a Chinese syllable, the pitch pattern: 四個聲調 "four tones", 聲調錯了 "the tone is wrong", 練習聲調. It can also mean the tone of someone's voice. 聲 "sound" has 耳 "ear" at the bottom; 調 is read diào here, not tiáo as in 調整 "adjust". For "intonation", Taiwan uses 語調.
column7: Chinese has four tones.

column3: Noise, unwanted loud sound: 噪音太大 "too noisy", 噪音污染, 製造噪音 "make noise". It is a measurable thing, for traffic, construction or neighbors. For a sound that is just loud, 吵 "noisy" is the verb. 噪 has 口 "mouth" and 喿, birds chirping together, and 音 is "sound".
column6: Wàimiàn de zàoyīn tài dà le.
column7: The noise outside is too loud.

column3: Audio system, stereo, the equipment: 一組音響 "a stereo set", 音響設備, 藍牙音響 "Bluetooth speaker". It can also mean the sound quality or acoustics: 音響效果. 音 is "sound" and 響 "to resound"; 響 has 音 under 鄉, which gives its sound (xiāng, now xiǎng).
column6: Tā mǎi le yī zǔ xīn yīnxiǎng.
column7: He bought a new stereo set.

column3: Sounds like, sounds as if: 聽起來很有趣 "sounds interesting", 聽起來不錯 "sounds good". It is followed by an adjective or 像: 聽起來像日文. The neutral tones are tīngqilai. It is about the impression from hearing something; for reading or looking, 看起來 "looks like" has the same shape.
column7: This idea sounds good.

column3: To broadcast, to play, to sow, mostly inside compounds: 播放 "play", 廣播 "broadcast", 播報 "report on air", 播種 "sow seeds". The dictionary records a fourth-tone reading, bò, for Taiwan. 扌 "hand" is the meaning part, and 番 stands for scattered seeds and also gives the sound.
column7: The television is playing the news.

column3: Leave a message or "a message left": 請留言 "please leave a message", 語音留言 "voicemail", 留言板 "message board", and online a "comment" under a post. It is not a spoken message left with a person; for that you say 轉告 or 請他回電. 留 "stay, leave behind" + 言 "words".
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǎngzhàn shàng liúyán.
column7: You can leave a message on the website.

column3: Teaching method, how a teacher teaches: 教法不同 "different methods", 這位老師的教法. The more usual full word is 教學法. 教 "teach" + 法 "method". 教 here is read in the fourth tone as part of a compound, while the verb "to teach" is jiāo.
column4: 这位老师的教法很特别。
column5: 這位老師的教法很特別。
column6: Zhè wèi lǎoshī de jiàofǎ hěn tèbié.
column7: This teacher's way of teaching is very special.

column3: Two readings, so watch the tone. As a verb, "to teach" is jiāo (first tone): 教中文 "teach Chinese". The fourth tone jiào is for "religion" (宗教), "teaching" in compounds (教育, 教室, 教授), and a spoken "to let, to tell": 教我怎麼做. 教 has 攵 "hand with a stick" and 孝 for the sound; 孝 sounds like xiào and the fit is rough.
column6: Wǒmen de jiàoshì zài sān lóu.
column7: Our classroom is on the third floor.

column3: Instruct, guide, teach morals, formal and respectful, mostly of an elder or teacher: 老師的教導 "the teacher's guidance", 父母的教導, 教導孩子. It is about character and values, more than about facts. 導 "lead" has 道 "path" over 寸 "hand": a hand showing the way.
column4: 我永远记得老师的教导。
column5: 我永遠記得老師的教導。
column6: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn jìde lǎoshī de jiàodǎo.
column7: I will always remember my teacher's guidance.

column3: New character, a character one has not yet learned: 學習生字 "learn new characters", 生字簿 "character workbook", and the 生字 of a lesson. 生 means "raw, unfamiliar" here, as in 生人 "stranger" and 陌生. A new word is 生詞. 字 is a child 子 under a roof 宀.
column4: 今天老师教了十个生字。
column5: 今天老師教了十個生字。
column6: Jīntiān lǎoshī jiāo le shí ge shēngzì.
column7: The teacher taught ten new characters today.

column3: Learn to, master: 學會游泳 "learn to swim", 學會了嗎？ "have you got it?", 學不會 "can't get it". The 會 on the end is the result: you can do it now. It differs from 學 "study", which says nothing about success. 學會 can also mean a "learned society": 學會會員.
column7: I finally learned to swim.

column3: In Taiwan, 國語 is the name for Mandarin Chinese, "the national language": 說國語 "speak Mandarin", 國語課 "Chinese class" in school. For teaching to foreigners, 華語 is used. It is not the same as 台語, Taiwanese Hokkien. 國 is a land with its borders 囗; 語 is 言 "speech" and 吾, which gives the sound.
column6: Tā de Guóyǔ shuō de hěn biāozhǔn.
column7: His Mandarin is very standard.

column3: Noun in grammar, and in general a "term": 名詞和動詞 "nouns and verbs", 專有名詞 "proper noun", 新名詞 "new term". 名 "name" + 詞 "word". 名 has 口 "mouth" and 夕 "evening": a name called out in the dark. 詞 has 言 "speech" and 司 as its sound.
column7: This term is hard to translate.

column3: Writing, language, culture, in compounds: 中文 "Chinese", 英文 "English", 作文 "composition", 文化 "culture", 文章 "article". Language names with 文 are the written or general language; 語 is spoken. The old shape is a tattooed chest, the same word as 紋 "pattern", and writing is seen as a pattern of marks.
column7: I am studying Chinese.

column3: Translate, seen in compounds: 翻譯 "translate", 譯成 "translate into", 中譯英 "Chinese to English", 譯者 "translator". 言 "speech" is the meaning part, and 睪 gives the sound (yì). Use 翻譯 for the plain verb.
column4: 这本书已经被译成英文。
column5: 這本書已經被譯成英文。
column6: Zhè běn shū yǐjīng bèi yìchéng Yīngwén.
column7: This book has already been translated into English.

column3: Housewife, a woman who manages the home: 家庭主婦 is the full and common form, and 全職主婦 "full-time homemaker". 主 is the lamp that stays at home, "master, host", and 婦 is a woman 女 with a broom 帚. Today many people avoid it because it implies she does no other job.
column7: My mom is a housewife.

column3: Air force: 空軍 is a branch of the armed forces, with 陸軍 "army" and 海軍 "navy" for the others. 他在空軍服務 "he serves in the air force". 空 is "empty, sky" and 軍 is an army, with 車 "chariot" under the cover 冖.
column7: He serves in the air force.

column3: Office worker, staff member, a person who works in an office or bank: 公司職員, 銀行職員, 一般職員. In speech, Taiwanese often say 上班族 for "office workers" in general. 職 means "post, duty" and has 耳 "ear" on the left, listening for orders; 員 is "member".
column7: He is a bank employee.

column3: Help, assist, mostly in compounds: 幫助 "help", 助手 "assistant", 助理 "assistant, aide", 協助 "assist", 助教 "teaching assistant". 力 "strength" is the meaning part, which fits; 且 is an old sound and no longer sounds alike. As a plain verb, "help" is 幫.
column7: Thank you for your help.

column3: Do things, "work" (in a job), or "handle matters": 做事很認真 "works seriously", 在公司做事 "work at a company", 做事情 is the longer form. It says how someone goes about tasks, so you can describe a person with it: 做事很細心. 做 has 亻 "person" and 故; 事 "matter" is a hand holding a flag.
column7: He works very seriously.

column3: Pencil. 鉛 "lead" and 筆 "writing brush, pen": the lead one. 用鉛筆寫 "write with a pencil", 削鉛筆 "sharpen a pencil", and 鉛筆盒 "pencil case". A ballpoint pen is 原子筆 in Taiwan. 筆 has 竹 "bamboo" over 聿, a hand holding a brush.
column7: Please write with a pencil.

column3: So-called, "what is called": 所謂的專家 "the so-called experts" (often mocking), and 所謂…就是… "what is called ... is ...", which defines a term: 所謂幸福，就是… . It is a written style, used in arguments and definitions. 所 makes a clause into a thing, and 謂 is "to call, to say".
column4: 所谓幸福，就是和家人在一起。
column5: 所謂幸福，就是和家人在一起。
column6: Suǒwèi xìngfú, jiùshì hé jiārén zài yīqǐ.
column7: What is called happiness is being together with family.

column3: As for, which brings up another topic: 至於他，我不知道 "as for him, I don't know". It often follows a first part that tells what one knows. Also in the structure 至於…就 and in a negative question: 不至於 "it won't come to that". Taiwan writes 於, not 于, in the traditional form.
column4: 我只知道这些，至于其他的我不清楚。
column5: 我只知道這些，至於其他的我不清楚。
column6: Wǒ zhǐ zhīdào zhèxiē, zhìyú qítā de wǒ bù qīngchu.
column7: I only know this much; as for the rest, I'm not sure.

column3: Change, alter, in official and written style: 變更日期 "change the date", 變更地址 "change the address", 變更計畫. It is for things like schedules and registrations, not changes in a person. 更 is read gēng here, "to change", not gèng "more".
column7: The meeting time has been changed.

column3: Fall behind, get worse, the opposite of 進步 "make progress": 成績退步 "grades have dropped", 退步了. Another meaning is "step back, make a concession" or "room to maneuver": 沒有退步的餘地. 退 has 辶 "move" and 艮 for the sound; 步 is two feet, one after the other.
column6: Tā zhè cì de chéngjì tuìbù le.
column7: His grades have dropped this time.

column3: Replace, take the place of: 機器取代人 "machines replace people", 被取代 "be replaced", 無法取代. The new thing is the subject, and the old is the object. 取 shows a hand taking an ear, from the custom of counting enemy ears; 代 is "in place of" with 亻.
column6: Shǒujī qǔdài le hěn duō dōngxi.
column7: Mobile phones have replaced many things.

column3: Use up, exhaust, to the limit, and as a prefix "all": 盡力 "do one's best", 用盡 "use up", 盡情 "to one's heart's content". In 盡量 "as much as possible" it is read jǐn. The character is a hand with a brush 聿 and the last drops of ink in a bowl 皿.
column7: I will do my best to help you.

column3: Not see, "be missing, gone": 好久不見 "long time no see", 不見面 "not meet". It means "to disappear" as well: 人不見了. In speech the 不 is said bú before the fourth-tone 見. 見 is an eye 目 on a person's legs 儿, someone who sees.
column7: Long time no see!

column3: Have disappeared, is gone: 我的手機不見了 "my phone is missing", 錢包不見了. It says that something that was there is no longer, often because it was lost. It is different from 丟了 "lost", which stresses the loss. For a missing person, 失蹤. 見 "see" + 了, the sense being "no longer seen".
column7: My phone is missing.

column3: Do, make, write, mostly in compounds: 工作 "work", 作業 "homework", 作文 "composition", 作用 "effect", 作家 "writer", 作為 "as". 作 and 做 are close, but 做 is the one for concrete things (做菜, 做事) and 作 for abstract or formal ones. 作 has 亻 "person" and 乍, which is a sound part and means "suddenly, newly made".
column6: Wǒ xiě wán zuòyè jiù shuìjiào.
column7: I go to sleep when I finish my homework.

column3: How one behaves as a person, one's conduct: 做人要誠實 "one must be honest", 做人處事 "conduct and dealing with people", 會做人 "know how to get along with people". It talks about character and manners. It does not mean "become a person". 做 "do" + 人 "person", the second a picture of a standing person seen from the side.
column7: One must be honest in life.

column3: Look after, take care of, give attention to: 顧小孩 "mind the children", 照顧 "take care of", 顧客 "customer", 顧不了那麼多 "can't care about all that". In Taiwan 顧 alone is a spoken verb with things like 顧店 "mind the shop". 頁 "head" is the meaning part, turning one's head to look, and 雇 gives the sound.
column4: 他一个人要顾三个孩子。
column5: 他一個人要顧三個孩子。
column6: Tā yī ge rén yào gù sān ge háizi.
column7: He has to look after three children by himself.

column3: Contribute, and "contribution": 對社會有貢獻 "contribute to society", 做出貢獻 "make a contribution", 貢獻心力. It is a respectful, written word for giving effort, time or talent for a group or cause. 貢 has 貝 "shell, money" and 工 for the sound, which is still near (gōng, gòng). 獻 "offer" has 犬 "dog".
column4: 他对社会有很大的贡献。
column5: 他對社會有很大的貢獻。
column6: Tā duì shèhuì yǒu hěn dà de gòngxiàn.
column7: He has made a great contribution to society.

column3: Assist, help, a formal word: 協助警方 "assist the police", 協助調查, 感謝您的協助 "thank you for your help". It is for helping with a task that someone else is in charge of, usually in an organization. 協 means "together" and has 十 and 劦 "work together"; 助 is "help".
column4: 请协助我们完成这件事。
column5: 請協助我們完成這件事。
column6: Qǐng xiézhù wǒmen wánchéng zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Please help us finish this matter.

column3: Usage, how something is used, for words, grammar and tools: 用法說明 "instructions for use", 這個字的用法, 詞語用法. Something with one meaning but many uses has several 用法. 用 "use" + 法 "method". The thing used goes before: 這個詞的用法.
column6: Zhège zì de yòngfǎ hěn tèbié.
column7: The usage of this character is very special.

column3: Rule, custom, and as an adjective "well-behaved": 守規矩 "follow the rules", 沒規矩 "have no manners", 規規矩矩 "properly". 規矩 means a compass and a set square, the tools that make a thing straight, and that is where "rules" come from. The second syllable is neutral: guīju. 規 has 見; 矩 has 矢 "arrow".
column7: You must follow the rules here.

column3: Limit, restrict: 限五人 "limited to five people", 每人限買兩個 "limit two per person", 限時 "time-limited", 以…為限 "up to". The thing limited goes before or after: 名額有限 "places are limited". 阝 here is the "mound, border" sign; it is on the left, and 艮 gives the sound (gèn, now xiàn).
column6: Měi rén xiàn mǎi liǎng ge.
column7: Limit two per person.

column3: According to, in written style: 據說 "it is said", 據報導 "according to reports", 根據 "based on", 據我所知 "as far as I know". It introduces a source of information at the start of a sentence. 據 has 扌 "hand", from the sense of "hold, rely on", and 豦 for the sound.
column4: 据新闻报导，明天会下雨。
column5: 據新聞報導，明天會下雨。
column6: Jù xīnwén bàodǎo, míngtiān huì xiàyǔ.
column7: According to the news, it will rain tomorrow.

column3: So as not to, lest: 早點出門，以免遲到 "leave early so as not to be late". It begins the second clause and names a bad result you want to avoid. The first clause says what to do. A good result is not used with it. 免 once showed a man in a ceremonial hat and came to mean "avoid".
column7: Leave early so as not to be late.

column3: Important, urgent, serious: 沒什麼要緊 "it's nothing serious", 要緊的事 "an urgent matter", 不要緊 "never mind". It is often negative: 不要緊 is a common reply to an apology. 要 "essential" + 緊 "tight, pressing"; 緊 has 糸 "thread" and 臤 for the sound.
column4: 这件事很要紧，不能忘记。
column5: 這件事很要緊，不能忘記。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn yàojǐn, bù néng wàngjì.
column7: This matter is important, and must not be forgotten.

column3: Such as, as, like: it introduces examples in written style: 水果，如蘋果、香蕉 "fruit, such as apples and bananas". It is also in 如果 "if", 例如 "for example", 如何 "how", 不如 "had better, not as good as". 如 has 女 and 口; as a stand-alone word it is formal, and speech uses 像 or 比如.
column4: 我喜欢水果，如苹果和香蕉。
column5: 我喜歡水果，如蘋果和香蕉。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan shuǐguǒ, rú píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo.
column7: I like fruit, such as apples and bananas.

column3: Even if, for a hypothetical condition that does not change the result: 就算下雨，我也要去 "even if it rains, I'll go". It goes with 也 or 還是 in the second clause. It is spoken. A close word is 即使, which is written. 算 "count" has 竹 over 具, an abacus-like picture.
column6: Jiùsuàn xiàyǔ, wǒ yě yào qù.
column7: Even if it rains, I will go.

column3: No matter what, in any case: 無論如何，我都會去 "whatever happens, I'll go". It often goes at the start, then 都 or 也. It states a firm decision or demand. Parts: 無論 "no matter" + 如何 "how". 無 is a person dancing with ox tails; 論 "discuss" has 言 "speech" and 侖.
column7: No matter what, I will go.

column3: Take advantage of (a time or chance): 趁熱吃 "eat it while it's hot", 趁年輕 "while one is young", 趁機會. It sets up a window of time that will close, followed by what to do in it. 趁 has 走 "walk, move" for its meaning and 㐱 for the sound.
column7: Eat it while it's hot.

column3: Can bear it, can stand it: 受得了 / 受不了 "can't stand it". The negative 受不了 is far more common in speech and is also used for annoyance: 吵死了，我受不了 "so noisy, I can't stand it". It is a result complement: 受 "receive, suffer" + 得 + 了 (liǎo). The neutral 得 means shòudeliǎo.
column4: 这么热的天气，你受得了吗？
column5: 這麼熱的天氣，你受得了嗎？
column6: Zhème rè de tiānqì, nǐ shòudeliǎo ma?
column7: Can you stand such hot weather?

column3: Be willing to: 肯 plus a verb. It is about willingness, often in the negative: 他不肯幫忙 "he refuses to help". It is also in 肯定 "definitely, to affirm" and 不肯. Unlike 願意, it suggests agreeing in spite of reluctance, or readiness to take the step. 肯 has 止 over ⺼ "flesh".
column7: He refuses to tell me.

column3: Best, optimal, formal: 最佳男主角 "best actor", 最佳選擇 "the best choice", 最佳時機 "the best moment". It is used in awards, advertising and advice. 最 "most" + 佳 "good". 佳 has 亻 "person" and 圭, which sounds alike (guī, jiā), and it is in 佳餚 and 佳節.
column7: This is the best choice.

column3: Obstacle, barrier: 語言障礙 "language barrier", 溝通障礙, 克服障礙 "overcome obstacles". In Taiwan 無障礙 means "barrier-free, accessible": 無障礙廁所. 障 has 阝 "wall, mound" for the sense of blocking, and 礙 has 石 "stone": a stone in the way. Written zhàng'ài with an apostrophe.
column6: Yǔyán bù shì wǒmen de zhàng'ài.
column7: Language is not our obstacle.

column3: Chaotic, in disorder: 交通混亂 "traffic chaos", 局勢混亂 "the situation is in chaos", 場面混亂. It describes a situation of confusion with people or things mixed in disorder. 混 "mix" has 氵 "water", things mixed together; 亂 shows hands unraveling a tangle.
column7: The roads are chaotic at rush hour.

column3: Full, fulfilling, rich in content: 生活很充實 "life is full", 內容充實 "substantial content". As a verb, "to enrich": 充實自己 "improve oneself". It is a good thing, a life with things to do. 充 "fill" + 實 "solid, real". The second has 宀 "roof" over a string of coins 貫.
column6: Wǒ de dàxué shēnghuó hěn chōngshí.
column7: My university life is very full.

column3: Level, standard of quality or skill: 水準很高 "a high standard", 生活水準 "living standard", 提高水準 "raise the standard". In Taiwan it is written 水準, not 水准. 準 shows water 氵 in a level: 水準 is the "level" of a spirit level, hence a measure for comparing quality.
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de shuǐzhǔn hěn gāo.
column7: This restaurant's standard is very high.

column3: Difference, between two things, in written or serious style: 文化差異 "cultural differences", 差異很大 "very different", 個別差異 "individual differences". The colloquial words are 不一樣 and 差別. 差 here is read chā "difference", not chà "poor" or chāi. 異 "different" is a person in a mask.
column4: 两个地方的文化差异很大。
column5: 兩個地方的文化差異很大。
column6: Liǎng ge dìfang de wénhuà chāyì hěn dà.
column7: The cultures of the two places are very different.

column3: Sincerity, "sincere": 真心話 "words from the heart", 真心喜歡 "really like", 一片真心 "all one's heart". It describes a feeling that is not put on. It can follow 的 as a noun or come before a verb: 真心想幫你. 真 "real" + 心 "heart", a picture of a heart.
column6: Wǒ shì zhēnxīn xiǎng bāng nǐ.
column7: I sincerely want to help you.

column3: Really, truly: 他真是個好人 "he is really a good person". In speech it also complains, and comes at the end or alone: 你真是的！ "honestly, you!", 真是的，又遲到了 "for goodness' sake, late again". The neutral 是 gives zhēnshi. The speaker is annoyed with someone present or absent.
column7: He is really a good person.

column3: Pretend: 假裝不知道 "pretend not to know", 假裝睡覺, 假裝生氣. The following verb is the act pretended. 假 is read jiǎ "fake" here, not jià "holiday". 裝 means "to dress up, to put on", and has 衣 "clothes" at the bottom.
column7: He pretended not to see me.

column3: Clear, clean, of water, air or an image, and "clear" as a verb: 水很清 "the water is clear", 看清 "see clearly", 清楚 "clear", 清潔 "clean", 清帳 "settle accounts". 氵 "water" is the meaning part, and 青 still gives the sound (qīng). Another character with the same parts is 情 "feeling".
column7: The water here is very clear.
