column3: Fortunately, for something that turned out well: 幸好你來了 "luckily you came", 幸好沒下雨. It is placed before the clause that turned out well, often giving a bad possibility that was avoided. 幸好 and 幸虧 can mostly be exchanged. 幸 is "luck", 好 "good".
column7: Fortunately I brought an umbrella.

column3: Luckily, thanks to: 幸虧你提醒我 "luckily you reminded me". It is like 幸好 but points to a cause: what saved the situation is named right after it, usually a person or an action. 幸虧 is a little stronger and is used more in writing. 虧 as a word is "to lose, to be short of".
column7: Luckily you reminded me.

column3: Seem, resemble, found in compounds: 似乎 "it seems", 好似 "just like", 相似 "similar", 類似 "similar to". In 似乎 it is formal and adds a note of doubt. 似的 (shìde) after a noun means "as if": 像雪似的. 似 has 亻 "person" and 以, which gives the sound.
column7: He seems to be very tired.

column3: With one's own hands, personally: 親手做 "make with one's own hands", 親手交給他 "hand it to him personally". It stresses that the person did the thing without help, and often puts feeling behind the act: a gift made, a meal cooked. 親 "close, personal" + 手 "hand".
column4: 这是妈妈亲手做的蛋糕。
column5: 這是媽媽親手做的蛋糕。
column6: Zhè shì māma qīnshǒu zuò de dàngāo.
column7: This is a cake Mom made with her own hands.

column3: With one's own eyes, personally: 親眼看到 "see with one's own eyes", 親眼所見. It is used to stress that one saw something and it is true. 親 "personal" + 眼 "eye"; 眼 has 目 "eye" with 艮, a sound part now far from yǎn.
column6: Wǒ qīnyǎn kànjiàn tā jìnqù le.
column7: I saw him go in with my own eyes.

column3: To someone's face, in person: 當面說 "say it to his face", 當面謝謝你 "thank you in person". The 當 is read dāng here ("facing"), not dàng. It can be about speaking directly in a good or bad sense, in person rather than through a message. 面 is a picture of a face.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng dāngmiàn gēn tā dàoxiè.
column7: I want to thank him in person.

column3: Specially, on purpose for it: 特地來看你 "came specially to see you", 特地為你準備. It says that the effort was made for this reason, often with a note of kindness or trouble taken. 特 has 牛 "ox" and 寺 for the sound; 地 is "ground", and here it is just a suffix.
column6: Tā tèdì cóng Táizhōng lái kàn wǒ.
column7: He came all the way from Taichung just to see me.

column3: On the way, while at it: 順便買 "pick up on the way", 順便問一下 "by the way, let me ask". It marks a second small task done while doing the first, without extra trouble. 便 is read biàn "convenient". 順 has 頁 "head" and 川 "river": flowing smoothly.
column4: 你出去的时候，顺便帮我买杯咖啡。
column5: 你出去的時候，順便幫我買杯咖啡。
column6: Nǐ chūqù de shíhou, shùnbiàn bāng wǒ mǎi bēi kāfēi.
column7: When you go out, get me a coffee while you're at it.

column3: Together, written style: 一同前往 "go together", 一同參加 "take part together". In speech people say 一起. It adds a sense of the same time and purpose. 一 "one" + 同 "same", so "together, as one".
column7: We go to see a film together.

column3: Same, and "with" in a written style: 同年 "the same year", 同班 "in the same class", 同學 "classmate", 同事 "colleague", 同意 "agree", 不同 "different". In everyday Taiwan speech "with" is 跟 or 和 rather than 同. 同 has the box 冂 with 口 "mouth" inside.
column7: He and I are in the same class.

column3: Think back, recall: 回想起來 "when I think back", 回想當時 "think back to that time". It is a deliberate look at the past. 回 "return" + 想 "think". 回 is drawn as a spiral coming back in; 想 has 心 "heart" under 相, which gives the sound.
column4: 回想起来，那是一段快乐的时光。
column5: 回想起來，那是一段快樂的時光。
column6: Huíxiǎng qǐlái, nà shì yī duàn kuàilè de shíguāng.
column7: Thinking back, it was a happy time.

column3: Imagine: 無法想像 "can't imagine", 想像一下 "just imagine", and "imagination" as a noun: 想像力. In Taiwan it is written 想像. 想 "think" and 像 "like, image": picture something in the mind. 像 has 亻 "person" and 象 "elephant" for the sound.
column4: 我无法想像没有手机的生活。
column5: 我無法想像沒有手機的生活。
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ xiǎngxiàng méiyǒu shǒujī de shēnghuó.
column7: I can't imagine life without a phone.

column3: Treat as, regard as: 把A當作B "treat A as B". 他把我當作朋友 "he treats me as a friend", 當作沒看見 "act as if one had not seen it". The 當 here is read dàng. 當成 is a similar word, and 當作 is common in writing. 作 "to be, to make".
column7: He treats me as a friend.

column3: Treat as, regard as, the same as 當作: 把A當做B, 他把我當做朋友, 當做沒看見 "act as if one did not see". The two spellings differ only in 做 and 作, which are close in meaning and used interchangeably here. The 當 is read dàng. 把 comes first, then the thing, then 當做, then what it is taken to be.
column4: 他把这里当做自己的家。
column5: 他把這裡當做自己的家。
column6: Tā bǎ zhèlǐ dàngzuò zìjǐ de jiā.
column7: He treats this place as his own home.

column3: Know, mostly in compounds: 知道 "know", 知識 "knowledge", 通知 "notify", 知名 "well-known", 無知 "ignorant". It is not a free verb in speech; use 知道. 知 has 矢 "arrow" and 口 "mouth"; the old character was the same as 智 "wise", which has a 日 under it.
column4: 学校通知我们明天不上课。
column5: 學校通知我們明天不上課。
column6: Xuéxiào tōngzhī wǒmen míngtiān bù shàngkè.
column7: The school told us there will be no class tomorrow.

column3: What one has learned from experience, one's takeaways or reflections: 學習心得 "study notes", 讀書心得 "reading report", 分享心得 "share one's insights", 心得報告 "a reflection paper". In Taiwanese schools students often have to write one. 心 "heart, mind" + 得 "gain".
column4: 他分享了学习中文的心得。
column5: 他分享了學習中文的心得。
column6: Tā fēnxiǎng le xuéxí Zhōngwén de xīndé.
column7: He shared what he has learned from studying Chinese.

column3: Kind intention, thoughtfulness, the feeling behind a gift or a favor: 一點心意 "a small token", 謝謝你的心意 "thank you for your thought", 這是我的心意. It is humble when you give something, and it is polite to accept it for the thought. 心 "heart" + 意 "intent": 意 has 心 under 音.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de yīdiǎn xīnyì.
column7: This is a small token from me.

column3: Wisdom, intelligence: 人生的智慧 "wisdom of life", 有智慧 "wise", 智慧財產權 "intellectual property". 智慧型手機 is Taiwan's word for a "smartphone". Both characters are about the mind: 智 is 知 "know" over 日; 慧 has 心 "heart" and 彗 for the sound (huì).
column7: Old people have rich wisdom.

column3: Philosophy: 哲學家 "philosopher", 哲學系 "philosophy department", 人生哲學 "philosophy of life". It names the field of study as well as a person's outlook. 哲 means "wise" and has 口 "mouth" with 折 for the sound; 學 "study" shows children 子 in a building.
column7: He studies philosophy at university.

column3: Role model, example to follow: 好榜樣 "a good example", 以…為榜樣 "take ... as a model", 做榜樣 "set an example". A person, usually someone older, fills this role. 榜 first meant a notice posted up, with 木 "wood" and 旁 for the sound; 樣 means "appearance".
column7: The older brother is the younger brother's role model.

column3: Religion: 宗教信仰 "religious belief", 你有宗教信仰嗎？ "do you have a religion?", 宗教自由. Taiwan is known for the mix of Buddhism, Daoism and folk faith. 宗 shows an altar 示 under a roof 宀, for ancestors; 教 "teaching" is read jiào here.
column4: 台湾有很多不同的宗教。
column5: 台灣有很多不同的宗教。
column6: Táiwān yǒu hěn duō bùtóng de zōngjiào.
column7: There are many different religions in Taiwan.

column3: Daoism, the religion based on 道 "the Way". In Taiwan it is practiced widely in temples (道教廟宇) and folk customs. 信道教 "believe in Daoism", 道士 "Daoist priest". 道 "way" has 辶 "move" and 首 "head"; 教 here is "religion", jiào. The founder's book is the 道德經.
column7: Many Taiwanese follow Daoism.

column3: Buddhism: 信佛教 "be Buddhist", 佛教徒 "Buddhist", 佛教寺廟. 佛 "Buddha" is read fó here and fú in the older literary 彷彿 "as if". Buddhism came to China from India, and 佛 was a sound-borrowed word for "Buddha": 亻 "person" with 弗 for the sound.
column7: He is Buddhist.

column3: Christianity, and in Taiwan usually Protestantism: Catholicism is 天主教, a separate word. 基督 is the sound-borrowed "Christ". 基督徒 "Christian", 基督教會. 基 "base" has 土 "earth" for the meaning and 其 for the sound; 教 here is "religion", jiào.
column7: Their family is Christian.

column3: God, in Taiwan the usual word in Protestant Christianity; 神 is also used, and Catholics say 天主. Older meaning: the supreme ruler of heaven in ancient China. 相信上帝 "believe in God", 感謝上帝. 上 "above" + 帝 "emperor". The word 帝 is in 皇帝 "emperor" and 帝國 "empire".
column7: He believes in God.

column3: Heaven, paradise, religious or figurative: 上天堂 "go to heaven", 天堂與地獄 "heaven and hell", 購物天堂 "a shopper's paradise", 美食天堂. 天 "sky" + 堂 "hall": the hall of heaven. 堂 has 土 for the meaning and 尚 for the sound. The word for a hell is 地獄.
column7: This place is a paradise for food.

column3: Soul, spirit: 靈魂 and 身體, 靈魂深處 "deep in the soul", 他有高貴的靈魂. It is a religious or literary word, also used for the essence of something: 這是球隊的靈魂人物 "the soul of the team". 魂 has 鬼 "ghost, spirit" and 云 for the sound; 靈 is "spirit, effective".
column7: He believes that people have a soul.

column3: Temple, especially a Chinese temple of Daoist and folk religion, with a deity: 媽祖廟 "Mazu temple", 去廟裡拜拜 "go to the temple to pray", 廟會 "temple fair". In Taiwan there are temples in every neighborhood, and they are part of everyday life. 廟 has 广 "building" and 朝.
column7: We go to the temple to worship.

column3: Temple in general, for Buddhist and Daoist places of worship: 參觀寺廟, 一座寺廟. 寺 is a Buddhist temple or monastery and 廟 a Daoist or folk temple, so 寺廟 covers both. 寺 shows 土 over 寸 "hand"; it is the sound part in 時 and 特, where it is read shí and tè.
column4: 这座寺庙已经有三百年的历史。
column5: 這座寺廟已經有三百年的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò sìmiào yǐjīng yǒu sān bǎi nián de lìshǐ.
column7: This temple has a history of three hundred years.

column3: Church: 去教堂做禮拜 "go to church for the service", 天主教堂 "Catholic church", 一座教堂. It is the building. The community is 教會. 教 here is "religion" (jiào), and 堂 is a hall, as in 禮堂 "auditorium" and 食堂 "canteen".
column7: They go to church on Sundays.

column3: Recommend: 推薦 plus the thing or person, and often a person to whom: 推薦一本書給我, 老師推薦我 "the teacher recommended me", 推薦信 "letter of recommendation". It is for suggesting something to others, from a good reason. 推 has 扌 "hand" and 隹; 薦 has 艹 "grass".
column4: 你可以推荐一本书给我吗？
column5: 你可以推薦一本書給我嗎？
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ tuījiàn yī běn shū gěi wǒ ma?
column7: Can you recommend a book to me?

column3: The truth, honest words: 說實話 "to tell the truth", 實話實說 "say it as it is", 老實話. 說實話 is often the start of a frank opinion: 說實話，我不喜歡. 實 "real" + 話 "words". 實 has 宀 "roof" over 貫 "string of coins", real wealth in the house.
column6: Shuō shíhuà, wǒ bù xǐhuan zhège.
column7: To tell the truth, I don't like this one.

column3: Field, domain, area of study or work: 專業領域 "professional field", 在…領域 "in the field of", 科學領域. It is a written word. 領 has 頁 "head" and 令; a neck and then "lead, guide". 域 has 土 "earth", a territory, with 或, the same part as in 國 "country".
column6: Tā shì zhège lǐngyù de zhuānjiā.
column7: He is an expert in this field.

column3: King: 國王 and 王后 "queen", the ruler of a kingdom. Taiwan has no king, so you meet the word in stories and news about other countries. 國 is a land 囗 with its borders; 王 is "king", once a picture of an axe, a sign of power.
column7: The king lives in a castle.

column3: Election: 總統選舉 "presidential election", 選舉日, 參加選舉, 選舉結果 "result". As a verb, "to elect": 選舉總統. Elections in Taiwan are a big public event, with campaigns and a vote. 選 "choose" and 舉 "raise": 舉 shows hands lifting, as in raising a hand to vote. For the plain verb "choose", say 選.
column4: 台湾的总统选举每四年一次。
column5: 台灣的總統選舉每四年一次。
column6: Táiwān de zǒngtǒng xuǎnjǔ měi sì nián yī cì.
column7: Taiwan's presidential election is held every four years.

column3: Revolution, and "to revolt": 工業革命 "Industrial Revolution", 革命家, 辛亥革命 "the Revolution of 1911". Its original sense was to withdraw the "mandate of heaven" and change dynasty. 革 is a stretched animal hide, "strip off, change"; 命 is "order, fate", an order given by the mouth 口.
column7: The Industrial Revolution changed the world.

column3: The Republic (of China), founded in 1912. In Taiwan, years are counted from it: 民國115年 is 2026. To convert, add 1911. Dates on forms, receipts and in the news use it: 民國一百一十五年. 民 "people" + 國 "country". Also the "Republic of China era" 民國時代, 1912-1949 on the mainland.
column4: 今年是民国一百一十五年。
column5: 今年是民國一百一十五年。
column7: This year is the 115th year of the Republic.

column3: Colony: 殖民地時期 "the colonial period", 前殖民地, 荷蘭的殖民地. Taiwan's history includes Dutch and Japanese rule, so the word comes up in school history. 殖民 "colonize" has 殖 (歹 "bone", 直) and 民 "people"; 殖 means "to grow, to breed" and is read zhí.
column4: 台湾曾经是荷兰的殖民地。
column5: 台灣曾經是荷蘭的殖民地。
column6: Táiwān céngjīng shì Hélán de zhímíndì.
column7: Taiwan was once a Dutch colony.

column3: Corruption, and "rotten, decayed": 政治腐敗 "political corruption", 食物腐敗 "food goes bad", 貪污腐敗. Both senses are common; the context makes it clear. 腐 has 肉 "meat" under 广, meat that goes off; 敗 means "to defeat, to spoil" and has 貝 and 攵 "tap".
column4: 政府腐败让人民很失望。
column5: 政府腐敗讓人民很失望。
column6: Zhèngfǔ fǔbài ràng rénmín hěn shīwàng.
column7: Government corruption disappoints the people greatly.

column3: Fight a war, go to war: 兩國打仗 "the two countries are at war", 打了三年仗 "fought for three years". It is a verb with its object, so the length goes between: 打了三年仗. For a fight between people, 打架. 打 has 扌 "hand" and 丁; 仗 has 亻 "person" and 丈, and means "weapons, a battle".
column7: The two countries went to war.

column3: Army, armed forces: 軍隊進入城市 "troops enter the city", 一支軍隊. It names the whole body of soldiers, a country's or a unit's. A single soldier is 軍人 or 士兵. 軍 has 車 "chariot" under a cover; 隊 "team" has 阝 "mound" and means a row or a squad.
column7: The troops entered the city.

column3: Robber, bandit, an armed one, a word from stories and the news: 強盜搶走了錢. In Taiwan, a robber who threatens people is usually 搶匪, and 強盜 sounds more old-fashioned. 強盜 is also in 強盜行為 "robbery". 強 "strong" is read qiáng here, as in 強大; 盜 means "to steal", as in 盜版 "pirated".
column6: Qiángdào qiǎngzǒu le tā de qián.
column7: The robbers took his money.

column3: Thief, who steals things quietly: 抓小偷 "catch a thief", 小偷偷走了 "the thief stole". A pickpocket is 扒手. A robber is 搶匪, who uses force. 小 "small" here is just the common prefix. 偷 "steal" has 亻 "person" and 俞 for the sound, and both characters are in the word.
column6: Xiǎotōu tōuzǒu le wǒ de qiánbāo.
column7: The thief stole my wallet.

column3: Commit, violate, offend: 犯錯 "make a mistake", 犯法 "break the law", 犯罪 "commit a crime", 犯人 "prisoner, offender", 犯規 "foul". As a verb it takes a bad act as object: you never 犯 something good. 犭 "dog" is the meaning part, an animal radical in wrong-doing words, and 㔾 is the sound.
column6: Měi ge rén dōu huì fàncuò.
column7: Everyone makes mistakes.

column3: Bully, pick on: 欺負人 "bully people", 被欺負 "be bullied", 欺負弱小. It is about someone stronger mistreating someone weaker, in a child's school too. The second syllable is neutral: qīfu. 欺 has 欠 "yawn, lack" and 其 for the sound; 負 "carry, bear" is the second part.
column7: He is often bullied by classmates.

column3: Sacrifice: to give up one's life or something valuable for others: 犧牲自己 "sacrifice oneself", 為國犧牲 "die for one's country", 犧牲睡眠 "give up sleep". As a noun it is the loss itself: 很大的犧牲. Both characters have 牛 "ox" in them, the sacrificial animal, with 羲 and 生 for the sounds.
column4: 他为了家人牺牲了很多。
column5: 他為了家人犧牲了很多。
column6: Tā wèile jiārén xīshēng le hěn duō.
column7: He gave up a lot for his family.

column3: Relatively, in comparison, and "relative": 相對來說 "relatively speaking", 相對於 "relative to", 相對的 "relative". The opposite is 絕對 "absolute". It also means "face each other": 相對而坐. 相 is read xiāng "mutual" here; it shows an eye 目 looking at a tree 木, "to observe".
column4: 相对来说，这里的房价比较便宜。
column5: 相對來說，這裡的房價比較便宜。
column6: Xiāngduì lái shuō, zhèlǐ de fángjià bǐjiào piányi.
column7: Relatively speaking, house prices here are cheaper.

column3: And, reach, in time for: the "and" is written, between nouns: 老師及學生 "teachers and students", and 以及 "as well as". It is also in 及格 "pass an exam", 來得及 "there's still time", 及時 "in time". 及 once showed a hand 又 catching a person, "reach, catch up".
column4: 老师及学生都可以参加。
column5: 老師及學生都可以參加。
column6: Lǎoshī jí xuésheng dōu kěyǐ cānjiā.
column7: Both teachers and students can take part.

column3: And, with in a formal or written style: 與…有關 "related to", 與…不同 "different from", 參與 "take part in", 你與我. In speech 和 or 跟 is used instead. Taiwan writes it 與; it sits between two nouns or before the other party: 這與我無關 "this has nothing to do with me". It can also mean "to give" in classical phrases.
column7: This has nothing to do with me.

column3: In short, to sum up: it opens a final sentence that gathers what was said: 總而言之，這次考試很難. The parts are 總 "all together", 而 "and", 言 "speak" and 之 "it": "to put it all in a word". It is a written and spoken summary-marker. 總 has 糸 "thread" and 悤 for the sound.
column4: 总而言之，这次考试很难。
column5: 總而言之，這次考試很難。
column6: Zǒng'éryánzhī, zhè cì kǎoshì hěn nán.
column7: In short, this exam was hard.

column3: Use, by means of, according to, in order to, at (a time): in 以前 "before", 以後 "after", 可以 "may", 以為 "think (wrongly)", 以…為… "take ... as ...", 以免 "lest". As a word of its own it is formal and introduces a means or a basis: 以第一名的成績 "with first place". 以 is a person 人 carrying something.
column4: 他以第一名的成绩毕业。
column5: 他以第一名的成績畢業。
column6: Tā yǐ dì yī míng de chéngjì bìyè.
column7: He graduated with the top grades.

column3: Pass through, undergo, "classic": 已經 "already", 經過 "pass through", 經常 "often", 經驗 "experience", 經濟 "economy", 佛經 "Buddhist scripture". In 已經 it is a very common word. 經 has 糸 "thread" and 巠 for the sound: it is the warp threads running lengthwise on a loom, hence "go through" and "classic works".
column7: I have already eaten.
